confirmed.title: DpProcess.__or__ walks the whole process tree on every composition, making heterogeneous accountant accumulation quadratic
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree with the prebuilt extension (.venv). Every link verified: _base.py:405-415 _has_same_repeated_pld materialises Repeated(self,count)._pld_cache_key(); _base.py:379 default _leaf_and_count returns (self,1) and neither Composed nor CachedProcess overrides it (only Repeated does, _repeated.py:51); Composed._pld_cache_key -> iter_cache_key (_composed.py:43-46) is a full stack walk that descends into CachedProcess.inner (_iter_cache_key.py:30-34); __or__ :499-503 calls it on the accumulated spine on EVERY composition. git show 4bfd0c16 confirms the exact swap from `if left_leaf == right_leaf` to `_has_same_repeated_pld`. Measured `Accountant() | poisson(gaussian(1.0+0.001*i), 0.01)`: n=125 0.064s, 250 0.241s, 500 0.929s, 1000 4.07s - clean 4x per doubling. Control with `DpProcess._has_same_repeated_pld = lambda self, other, count: self is other or self == other`: 200 0.0033s, 400 0.0063s, 800 0.0095s, 1600 0.0193s, 3200 0.0392s - linear. Homogeneous path unaffected: 20000 identical compositions in 0.075s. Verified the DPTrainer is on the homogeneous path (_dp_trainer.py:287 `ctx.accounting |= ctx.step_process` with a single reused step object; the periodic `acc.cached(...)` wraps leave the spine bounded). Severity stays low: no wrong result, no epsilon change, and the documented loop in Accountant's docstring and docs/reference/accounting.md is homogeneous, so only a per-step-varying schedule pays. Not a duplicate of #911 (that issue is Monte Carlo calibration cost, a different code path).
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: A research script or per-step noise schedule folds heterogeneous steps into an Accountant: `for i in range(N): acct = acct | dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(sigma_i), q)`. No two steps merge, so the Composed spine grows and each `|` re-walks it via Repeated(spine, 2)._pld_cache_key(). Measured on this tree: 250 steps 0.24s, 500 steps 0.93s, 1000 steps 4.07s (quadratic), versus 0.003-0.04s for 200-3200 steps with the pre-#883 equality test (linear). Extrapolating the fitted quadratic, 10,000 heterogeneous steps costs several minutes and 50,000 costs hours of pure bookkeeping, with no warning and no indication the cost is in `|`. Results are numerically unchanged; the DPTrainer and any loop reusing one step object are unaffected.

confirmed.title: calibrate()'s runtime-safety fallback re-runs the whole adaptive search without the union bound, while still reporting the undivided mc_failure_probability
confirmed.reasoning: Verified in source and reproduced on a REAL Monte Carlo mechanism, not just a stub. Source: calibration.py:301-309 builds probe_config with mc_failure_probability/(max_iterations+2) and runs the first bisection under it; :321-323 opens `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`; :331-339 re-runs the FULL `_calibrate_impl` inside that context when the runtime re-evaluation is unsafe, and takes `achieved = result.achieved` from that second adaptive search; :350-351 stamps `result.mc_failure_probability = overall_config.mc_failure_probability` whenever the final PLD is MC-backed, regardless of which branch ran. So the union bound the code deliberately applies to the first search is dropped for the second, while mc_confidence still claims to cover it. Real-mechanism repro (b_min_sep BandMF, bands=4, n_steps=40, epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-3), mc_resolution=5e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-2, max_iterations=30, spy on Budget.evaluate): the fallback fired in 6 of 10 seed/p0 combinations, each time with ~25-30 probes at beta/32 followed by ~25-29 probes at the FULL beta=0.01, e.g. Counter({0.0003125: 28, 0.01: 28}), and the returned result reported mc_confidence=0.990000. The honest simultaneous bound for that fallback search is 1 - 28*0.01 = 0.72. Default-config arithmetic in the finding also checks out: resolved_num_mc_samples is 2,940,252 at beta=1e-6 and 3,417,797 at beta=1e-6/102, so probe-vs-runtime differences are estimation noise with no systematic sign, which is why the fallback fires roughly half the time. docs/reference/accounting.md:731-734 states verbatim the property the fallback discards ('result.mc_confidence therefore covers the adaptive search as a whole'). Severity medium, not high: the error is in the reported confidence level attached to epsilon, not in epsilon itself, and it only affects MC-backed processes (b_min_sep, balls_in_bins, MF Gaussian with MC PLDs); but the direction is fail-open and the overstatement is 25-100x. The secondary 'roughly doubles the probe count' observation overlaps open issue #911 (Monte Carlo calibration performance), but the confidence-accounting defect is distinct and not tracked there, so already_tracked is 0.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Calibrating any Monte-Carlo-backed process (e.g. BandMF + b_min_sep) with calibrate(). Roughly half the time the probe-config bisection's result is not privacy-safe when re-evaluated under the runtime discretization, and calibrate() silently re-runs the entire bisection under overall_config, i.e. with EVERY probe at the full mc_failure_probability instead of beta/(max_iterations+2). The returned param and achieved then come from that unprotected adaptive search, yet result.mc_confidence still reports 1 - beta. Observed directly: b_min_sep at beta=1e-2, max_iterations=30 ran 28 probes at 3.125e-4 followed by 28 probes at 1e-2 and returned mc_confidence=0.99, where the simultaneous bound over the 28 deciding probes is at best 0.72. At the library defaults (beta=1e-6, max_iterations=100) a team publishing 'epsilon = 3.0 at delta = 1e-5 with Monte-Carlo confidence 1 - 1e-6' from result.mc_confidence is overstating that confidence by up to ~100x on the fail-open side. Epsilon itself is unchanged; the failure probability attached to it is understated.

confirmed.title: CalibrateResult.achieved can violate the documented isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance) contract while reporting converged=True
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced twice: once with a stub budget and once with a real Monte Carlo mechanism. Source verified: calibration.py:324-325 computes `achieved = budget.evaluate(final_process)` under overall_config; :326-330 re-checks only privacy-safety; :340 `result.achieved = achieved` overwrites the converged probe value with no closeness re-check; _calibrate_impl (:474-534) hard-codes converged=True and is the only place the isclose test is applied. Both docstrings (calibration.py:136-142) and docs/reference/accounting.md:722-725 ('math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0) is true') still assert the old invariant. Stub repro: CalibrateResult(param=1.000000, achieved=0.500000, target=1.000000, iterations=1, converged), isclose False. Real-mechanism repro (b_min_sep BandMF bands=4, n_steps=40, epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-3), tolerance=1e-6): in the four of ten seed/p0 combinations where the fallback did NOT fire, achieved came back as 2.9768990653998104, 2.999839744431425, 2.9858047534416134 and 2.982586082209384 against target 3.0 - drifts of 5e-5 to 8e-3 relative, all failing isclose at rel_tol=1e-6 while converged=True. Direction is always privacy-safe (achieved <= target is re-checked at :326-330), so no under-noising; the defect is the contract and the reported convergence quality. Severity low: no epsilon or privacy impact, and the existing test test_reported_achieved_is_runtime_upper_bound only asserts achieved <= target and equality with the runtime re-evaluation, so nothing in the suite catches the broken isclose claim.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: For any Monte-Carlo-backed process, calibrate() returns converged=True with an `achieved` that is a fresh runtime-discretization re-measurement rather than the converged probe, so the documented postcondition math.isclose(achieved, target, rel_tol=tolerance, abs_tol=0.0) is false. Measured on b_min_sep BandMF at tolerance=1e-6 and target epsilon 3.0: achieved 2.9769 / 2.9826 / 2.9858 / 2.9998 in the four of ten runs that did not take the recalibration fallback - relative gaps of 5e-5 to 8e-3 against a 1e-6 tolerance. A downstream assertion of the documented contract fails, and a run card claiming 'calibrated to within 1e-6 of the target' is wrong by up to ~0.8%. The direction is privacy-safe (over-noised), so no epsilon guarantee is broken.

confirmed.title: A checkpoint budget silently overrides a stricter template budget on Accountant restore, leaving budget_exceeded on the looser cap
confirmed.reasoning: The mechanics reproduce exactly as claimed: saving Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(10.0, delta=1e-5)) after 5 x eps_delta(0.5, 1e-7) and restoring into Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)) yields restored._budget == EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-05), epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.499990499950025 and budget_exceeded == False. Source confirmed at _accountant.py:238-250 (checkpoint budget unconditionally replaces the template's, with only logger.warning) and :207-224 (budget_exceeded returns False for `self._budget is None` with no tri-state). I could not confirm this is a DEFECT rather than a deliberate design choice, which is why this is PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED: (a) packages/opaque-accounting/tests/test_budget_serialization.py:85-99 explicitly pins checkpoint-wins plus the warning as intended behaviour; (b) the warning does reach stderr in a bare process via logging's lastResort handler - I saw it in the repro - so 'silently' overstates the case; (c) no documented contract is violated: docs/reference/accounting.md:74-93 covers budget checkpoint codecs but says nothing about template-vs-checkpoint precedence; (d) I verified the DPTrainer is unaffected - it constructs bare Accountant() at _dp_trainer.py:280-281 and restores with opaque_from_state_dict(Accountant(), ...) at :5537, so no budget key is ever written or restored there. What remains is a genuine asymmetry (template wins when the checkpoint has no budget, loses when it has one) and the unlanded half of the OPQ-302 fix sketch, i.e. budget_exceeded still cannot distinguish 'no cap configured' from 'my cap was replaced'. That is a defensible API-hardening request, not a demonstrated fail-open bug.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: A caller resumes with `from_state_dict(Accountant(budget=epsilon_budget(1.0, delta=1e-5)), saved)` where the checkpoint was written by an accountant carrying epsilon_budget(10.0, delta=1e-5). The restored accountant keeps the checkpoint's looser cap: restored._budget == EpsilonBudget(10.0, 1e-05), epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.4999905, budget_exceeded == False, so a `while not acct.budget_exceeded` loop runs well past the intended epsilon <= 1.0. A WARNING line naming both budgets is emitted (and reaches stderr by default), and an explicit test pins this precedence as intended, so the operator is not left with no signal at all - the exposure is limited to harnesses that suppress or never read WARNING logs, and only when the caller deliberately passes a different budget on restore. The DPTrainer resume path never writes a budget key and is not affected.

confirmed.title: The exception taxonomy inverts two pre-existing error relationships it claims to preserve, breaking except-clauses without a breaking-change marker
confirmed.reasoning: The two behavioral inversions are real and I reproduced one directly. Baseline `git show 4b13d82:.../calibration.py` line 489 is `raise RuntimeError("Calibration for {budget.name} did not converge...")`; the current tree (calibration.py:537) raises CalibrationError, which via ConfigurationError derives from ValueError only (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27,38). Baseline `_budgets.py:311` is `raise TypeError(...)` for an unregistered budget type; the current tree raises CheckpointError, and I executed `budget_state_dict(Foo())` in the repo venv: `CheckpointError TypeError? False RuntimeError? True ValueError? False`. The change shipped in a released line, not just on a dev branch: `git describe 7b26f655` = v0.15.3-9, and `git tag --contains 7b26f655` lists v0.15.4, v0.15.5, v0.15.5.rc1/rc2, v0.15.6.rc1 - so v0.15.3 users who caught RuntimeError from calibrate() or ValueError/TypeError from the codec see those handlers stop firing on v0.15.4, and the commit subject is a plain `feat(...)` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's framing. (1) The docstring quote is selective: packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/exceptions/__init__.py:4-7 reads in full 'They preserve familiar Python error relationships: configuration, calibration, and privacy-budget errors are ValueError subclasses, while checkpoint failures are RuntimeError subclasses.' - it accurately documents the shipped taxonomy and does not claim the previous raise types were kept. docs/reference/exceptions.md carries the same correct mapping table. So the 'the docstring says it preserves and it doesn't' half of the title is wrong; only the silent-migration half survives. (2) This is a 0.x, Development Status 3 - Alpha library, so the release-contract argument is weaker than the finding implies. Severity stays low; no epsilon effect.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Between v0.15.3 and v0.15.4 (commit 7b26f655, titled `feat(exceptions): ...` with no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer) two exception families changed base class in incompatible directions. Non-convergence in `calibrate()` went from RuntimeError to CalibrationError (a ValueError subclass, NOT a RuntimeError); the accounting checkpoint/codec sites went from ValueError, and `budget_state_dict` on an unregistered type from TypeError, to CheckpointError (a RuntimeError subclass, NOT a ValueError or TypeError) - verified by execution: `budget_state_dict(Foo())` raises CheckpointError with isinstance(TypeError)=False, isinstance(RuntimeError)=True. Downstream v0.15.3 code doing `except RuntimeError:` around calibrate(), or `except ValueError:` around checkpoint restore, silently stops catching and the job crashes instead of taking its recovery path. Mitigations: the new taxonomy is fully and correctly documented (opaque/exceptions/__init__.py docstring and docs/reference/exceptions.md both state checkpoint -> RuntimeError, calibration -> ValueError), and the project is 0.x alpha, so the only concrete gap is the missing breaking-change marker/release note, not a wrong description of current behavior.

confirmed.title: Monte Carlo shard seeds alias across nearby user seeds: seeds S and S+2 share all but one shard of the transcript corpus
confirmed.reasoning: Verified by code reading and independently reproduced numerically. packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/b_min_sep/mc.rs:34-37 is `seed.wrapping_add((shard as u64).wrapping_mul(2)).wrapping_add(direction as u64)`, and balls_in_bins/monte_carlo.rs:50-55 is the same arithmetic with a bool direction. Trivially shard_seed(S, k, d) == shard_seed(S+2, k-1, d) for all k>=1. I checked that the alias actually propagates: the RNG is the only per-shard state, built as `StdRng::seed_from_u64(shard_seed(...))` at mc.rs:221/237/396/423 and monte_carlo.rs:205/229, and inside each `par_chunks_mut(...).enumerate()` closure `shard` is used for nothing but the seed - every other input (strategy_coef/gram, sigma, p, n_steps, chol) is shard-independent - so shard k of run S is bit-identical to shard k-1 of run S+2. samples_to_pmf sorts the sample vector (monte_carlo.rs:314), so the PMF is a function of the multiset and shared shards flow straight into the reported epsilon. Numerically reproduced against the prebuilt extension in the repo venv (b_min_sep over band_mf_strategy(bands=2), n_steps=40, p0=0.05, nm=1.0, discretization=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3 -> resolved_num_mc_samples=17354 = 17 shards): seeds 1000,1002,...,1010 give eps_at(1e-2) = 1.29801422, 1.29974058, 1.30809399, 1.31104217, 1.30283726, 1.30377245 (stdev 0.00493), while seeds 1000,2000,...,6000 give 1.29801422, 1.31705101, 1.26226398, 1.31656696, 1.33825894, 1.31136316 (stdev 0.02557) - a 5.2x collapse in spread, the same effect the finding reports with a different strategy. I also confirmed the default config really is 2872 shards (resolved_num_mc_samples = 2940252). The crate test `shard_seeds_separate_adjacency_directions` (mc.rs:710-721) only asserts within-run uniqueness, so nothing in-tree catches it. Severity low is right: each individual run still carries its own simultaneous confidence band, no reported epsilon is unsound, and the .pyi documents `seed` only as reproducibility, never independence. It degrades seed-sweeping as a stability diagnostic.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Because shard_seed is plain addition (seed + 2*shard + direction) and the shard index feeds nothing else, run S and run S+2 draw identical samples for all but one shard in each adjacency direction - at the default discretization config that is 2871 of 2872 shards, so stride-2 seeds are effectively the same estimate. Independently measured at 17 shards (b_min_sep, band_mf_strategy(bands=2), n_steps=40, p0=0.05, nm=1.0, disc=1e-3, mc_resolution=1e-3, mc_failure_probability=1e-3): stride-2 seeds 1000..1010 give epsilon_at(1e-2) stdev 0.00493 versus stdev 0.02557 for stride-1000 seeds - 5.2x too tight. A user who reruns the accountant at seeds 1000, 1002, 1004 to gauge Monte Carlo noise sees an artificially tight cluster and overestimates the stability of the bound. It also means an independently 'reproduced' (epsilon, delta, seed) triple at a nearby seed is not independent evidence. No individual reported epsilon is invalidated: each run still carries its own simultaneous KL confidence band, and the public docs promise only reproducibility from the seed, not independence. Both MC accountants (b-min-sep for BandMF, balls-in-bins for the correlated-noise MF mechanisms) share the arithmetic.

confirmed.title: dpsgd_acc.poisson() lost its inner-mechanism guard and now silently amplifies already-amplified and whole-horizon processes
confirmed.reasoning: Fully reproduced, including all four numbers, which matched to every printed digit. Baseline `git show 4b13d82:.../dpsgd/amplification/_poisson.py` has `_Inner = Gaussian | AdaClip | NonPrivate` and a factory-level `match inner: case Gaussian() | AdaClip() | NonPrivate(): pass; case _: raise TypeError('poisson() requires a Gaussian, AdaClip, or NonPrivate inner mechanism, ...')`. The current file has `_Inner = DpProcess` (:21), `__post_init__` checks only `isinstance(self.inner, DpProcess)` (:39-46), the type guard survives only inside the truncated branch (:91-98), and the non-truncated path falls through to `_native.poisson_pld(self.inner.pld(...), self.sample_rate)` (:162-173). Executed in the repo venv: `single = poisson(gaussian(1.1), 0.01)`; `(single*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 1.5154423566628403`; `(poisson(single, 0.01)*1000).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009836885508304796` (154.06x understatement, no error, no warning). `kt = k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block')` gives 0.970343695110472 alone and `poisson(kt, 0.1)` gives 0.10865088995647369. The asymmetry with the DP-FTRL sibling is real: packages/opaque-dpftrl/.../amplification/_poisson.py:279-288 still raises InputTypeError unless inner is MfGaussian with a BandMf/Identity strategy. TWO MITIGATING FACTS I established that the finding does not mention. (1) The generalization was deliberate and documented, not an accident: 3b22a6af updated docs/reference/accounting.md and docs/user-guide/accounting.md to say 'Plain Poisson accepts any Opaque DpProcess as its base mechanism', and added tests for the intended use (`poisson(acc.eps_delta(0.3), 0.2)`), replacing the old `test_rejects_non_gaussian` with `test_rejects_non_process`. (2) The open-algebra footgun is not unique to poisson: I checked that `kt * 10` on a whole-horizon k-out-of-t process is likewise accepted and returns 3.0968460135957514 with no guard, so the composition layer generally lets users build unrealizable expressions. That keeps this at medium rather than high: the documented DP-SGD path is unchanged and correct, and triggering the understatement requires the user to write an expression no Opaque sampler realizes. It stays at medium rather than low because a guard that specifically existed to catch this exact mistake was removed, the failure direction is epsilon understatement, and double-wrapping is a realistic slip in helper- or config-driven pipelines.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: The factory guard that used to reject non-Gaussian inners was removed in 3b22a6af as part of a deliberate, documented generalization to any DpProcess, but nothing replaced it for inners that are themselves participation models or compositions. Reproduced on the current tree: `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), 0.01), 0.01) * 1000` reports epsilon_at(1e-5) = 0.009837 where the correct single-amplification DP-SGD figure is 1.515442 - a 154x understatement with no error and no warning, where the pre-3b22a6af tree raised TypeError. Likewise `dpsgd_acc.poisson(dpsgd_acc.k_out_of_t(dpsgd_acc.gaussian(1.1), k=2, t=100, allocation='block'), 0.1)` reports 0.108651 against the 0.970344 the horizon process reports alone, for a mechanism ('Poisson-subsample the dataset, then run k-out-of-t on the subsample') that no Opaque sampler implements. A user who reaches that expression through a wrapper or config path and calibrates noise against it deploys at far less noise than their claimed epsilon requires. Scope limits: the documented single-amplification path (`poisson(gaussian(nm), q) * T`) is unchanged and correct; triggering this needs a user-constructed expression; and the composition layer is permissive elsewhere too (`k_out_of_t(...) * 10` is also accepted without a guard, returning 3.096846). The DP-FTRL sibling `dpftrl_acc.poisson` still enforces an MfGaussian inner, so the two stacks now disagree on strictness.

confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: With clipping_mode='adaptive' and sampling_mode='k_out_of_t' the accountant is handed expected_batch_size = train_batch_size while the sampler draws batches averaging dataset_size*k/n_steps. confirmed.title: the #881 random-allocation memoisation never serves a hit because epsilon_at folds a Monte-Carlo-only field into its cache key
confirmed.reasoning: The substantive claim reproduces. epoch_pld (packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:29-46) is an lru_cache keyed on the whole frozen DiscretizationConfig, which includes mc_resolution and mc_failure_probability (discretization.py:17-40, frozen dataclass -> those fields are in __eq__/__hash__). DpProcess.epsilon_at (_base.py:212-227) recomputes mc_resolution = min(configured, delta/2.0) and passes it down, while delta_at does not, so each distinct delta yields a distinct config and therefore a distinct epoch_pld key. The Rust transform is delta- and MC-independent: random_allocation.rs:164-227 plus Accuracy::derive/alloc_remove/alloc_add read only discretization, log_mass_truncation_bound, max_conv_grid, max_grid_size and tail_mass_truncation - no mc_* field is touched. The per-process pld_cache (_pld_cache.py) keys on the same config object, so it misses in lockstep. Measured (k=8, t=512, default discretization, prebuilt native ext): eps(1e-5) 16.52s misses=1; eps(1e-5) repeat 0.01s; eps(1e-6) 16.64s misses=2 hits=0; delta_at(3.0) 16.54s misses=3 hits=0. So a delta sweep re-pays the full O(G^2) transform for a result that cannot depend on delta. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding as written: (a) the title's 'never serves a hit' is false - I observed hits=1 when a structurally different process (allocation='total' at the same nm/k/t) queried the same delta, so epoch_pld does deduplicate across distinct processes at a fixed delta; its only useless dimension is delta; (b) the reported delta_at(3.0) value of 6.67e-09 did not reproduce - I measured 0.0 at that configuration (immaterial to the defect). No privacy impact; pure wasted work. Not a duplicate of open #911, which is about Monte Carlo calibration cost, not this deterministic transform.

U2...' where the canonical template emits '...A1</s>
<|user|>
U2...', and the trailing newline is also lost. One whitespace token per assistant turn. The assistant mask is unaffected and _generation_block_marks_only_assistant never compares the two renders, so nothing warns. The fine-tuned checkpoint is self-consistent (DPTrainer saves the mutated tokenizer), so the mismatch materialises only for a consumer that renders with the base model's original template - and the saved artifact's chat_template silently differs from the upstream one it was derived from.

confirmed.title: language_modeling_collator(completion_only_loss=True) now silently supervises the full sequence for rows that carry no completion_mask

confirmed.title: compute_loss_func is now invoked at two different tensor ranks; a per-example loss silently reports a different eval objective
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced numerically. The two call sites are as claimed: _dp_trainer.py:2719-2726 calls `self._compute_loss_func(output, custom_labels)` on the BATCHED forward output in the default eval branch, while _dp_trainer.py:2452-2456 (compute_per_example_loss) calls the same callable under vmap with the leading batch dim stripped -- its own docstring at :2409-2412 says 'One example's input dict (under vmap; the caller stripped the leading batch dim)'. `git show 25bb4ed7` ('fix(transformers): honor custom loss during evaluation (#1028)') confirms the batched branch previously read `output.get('loss')` and carried a comment telling users to set include_for_metrics=['loss'] to get compute_loss_func honoured at eval; that comment and the guard were removed. Nothing validates the rank of the callable's inputs or of its return. My repro (T=V=4, plain dict-returning nn.Module, compute_loss_func = lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:]), the documented per-example causal-LM shift): default evaluate() -> eval_loss 1.34594; include_for_metrics=['loss'] evaluate() -> 1.70644; hand-computed mean of per-example shifted CE over the same eval set -> 1.70644. So the default path is off by 0.36 nats with no exception, because the callable shifted along the batch axis and cross_entropy read the sequence axis as the class axis. Changing only V to 5 (T!=V) turns the same default eval into `RuntimeError: Expected target size [3, 5], got [3, 4]`, confirming the second half of the claim. The doc drift is real: docs/alignment/trainers.md:112-114 still says the SFT custom loss 'runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op', and packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:646-656 delegates every non-DFT loss_type to `super().prediction_step`, landing on the batched call. The tests added by 25bb4ed7 use only rank-agnostic losses (`cross_entropy(output['logits'], labels)` on 2-D logits), so none of them catch it. One correction: the token-weighted aggregation at :2946-2966 is now additionally gated on `self._is_causal_lm` (added by the same commit), so the compounding the finding describes applies to real HF causal LMs but not to the plain module I used -- I verified the gate exists but did not separately measure the token-weighting amplification. Severity medium: it requires a user-supplied compute_loss_func that is sensitive to the leading axis, affects only reported eval metrics (and through them best-model selection / early stopping), and has no effect on the training objective, gradients, noise or epsilon.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: A user passes `compute_loss_func=lambda out, labels: F.cross_entropy(out['logits'][:-1], labels[1:])` -- the per-example causal-LM shift that the documented contract (compute_per_example_loss docstring at _dp_trainer.py:2409-2412 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:114, 'it runs inside vmap, so it must be a pure per-example op') tells them to write. Training invokes it per example under vmap; since 25bb4ed7 (#1028) the DEFAULT eval path invokes the same callable once on the batched ModelOutput at _dp_trainer.py:2719-2726, with no rank check. Measured on a 16-example eval set with T=V=4: the true training objective (and the include_for_metrics=['loss'] eval path) is 1.70644, while the default evaluate() reports eval_loss 1.34594 -- a silent ~0.36-nat divergence, because the slice shifted the batch axis and cross_entropy treated the sequence axis as classes. With metric_for_best_model='eval_loss' / load_best_model_at_end / early stopping, the wrong series drives checkpoint selection. When T != V the identical configuration instead raises `RuntimeError: Expected target size [3, 5], got [3, 4]` at eval, so a user whose custom loss previously worked (the batched branch used to ignore compute_loss_func and read output['loss']) now gets a crash. Eval metrics only: no effect on gradients, clipping, noise or the privacy accounting. SFT with loss_type in {'nll','chunked_nll'} reaches the same batched call via _sft_trainer.py:646-656.

confirmed.title: Compact SDPA sliding-window elision reopens OPQ-337: gemma2 with softcapping disabled attends to the full context

With the default softcapping of 50.0 the patched path is correct. (b) Mistral/Ministral with attention_dropout != 0 evaluated in .train() under torch.no_grad(): the mask builder elides the window because grad is disabled while the patched SDPA forward declines to apply it because runtime dropout != 0, so the window is again lost (patched 11.734835026116343 == no-window control, upstream 11.663893043994904). confirmed.title: Public install documentation's "Extras" commands omit the registry index and resolve to an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Docs verified: README.md:67-72 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:19-27 teach `pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` (and the uv `--index` form), and the Extras blocks immediately below (README.md:78-81, installation.md:33-36) show four bare commands with no index flag: `pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`. A grep for packages.jetbrains.team across README.md and docs/ returns only those four lines (README:68,72 and installation:20,27) — every other install instruction is bare, including docs/user-guide/index.md:9 ('Install with `pip install opaque` (plus `opaque[...]` extras)') and docs/alignment/trainers.md:319 (`pip install opaque[trl]`), which the finding did not list. PyPI `opaque` is confirmed to be version 1.0.0 'python libopaque wrapper' by Stefan Marsiske, while the real project is served only from the JetBrains index (verified: that simple index lists real opaque wheels anonymously). Actual reproduction in a clean venv: `pip install --dry-run "opaque[all]"` printed only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'` and resolved to `Would install opaque-1.0.0 pysodium-0.7.18`, building the unrelated sdist's metadata in the process. I then installed a stand-in real `opaque` 0.15.0 (with auditing/all extras) into the same venv and re-ran: pip still reported `Would install opaque-1.0.0`, i.e. the extras command does replace an already-installed real Opaque, whereas the bare `pip install opaque` in the same state was a no-op ('Requirement already satisfied ... 0.15.0'). So the finding's 'overwrites the installed opaque distribution' claim is accurate specifically for the extras form. Severity kept at medium: the outcome is a broken/wrong environment with only a warning, it is fully user-visible on the next import, and no privacy guarantee is affected.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: A reader following README.md or docs/getting-started/installation.md top to bottom installs the real Opaque from the JetBrains index, then copies the Extras line below it. Because `--index-url` does not persist across invocations, `pip install "opaque[all]"` resolves from PyPI, where `opaque` is an unrelated 'python libopaque wrapper' 1.0.0. Reproduced in a clean venv with pip 24.0: the command emits only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'` and resolves to opaque-1.0.0 + pysodium-0.7.18; with a real `opaque` 0.15.0 already installed it still resolves to opaque-1.0.0, replacing it (the bare `pip install opaque` in the same state is a no-op instead). The user's `import opaque.dpsgd` then breaks, or a CI image built from these docs ends up with the wrong `opaque` distribution. Same hazard for `uv add`, and the same missing flag appears in docs/user-guide/index.md:9 and docs/alignment/trainers.md:319.

confirmed.title: The committed uv.lock still resolves accelerate 1.14.0, which carries an open GitHub-reviewed advisory with a released fix
confirmed.reasoning: Independently reproduced. /home/user/opaque/uv.lock:40-56 pins accelerate 1.14.0. I re-ran an OSV querybatch over all registry-sourced packages in uv.lock myself (217 entries, not 218) and got exactly one hit: accelerate 1.14.0 -> GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 / PYSEC-2026-3804 / CVE-2026-69112, MODERATE, github_reviewed_at 2026-09-08, CWE-22, ranges {introduced 0, last_affected 1.14.0}. OSV returns {} for accelerate 1.15.0, and PyPI confirms 1.15.0 exists (uploaded 2026-09-09), so a fixed version is available. uv.lock:2862 / :4146 confirm accelerate is pulled transitively by peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0. .github/dependabot.yml:47-66 is as described (uv ecosystem, versioning-strategy lockfile-only, groups: workspace-dependencies patterns ["*"], weekly Monday). So the factual core of the finding holds. BUT the framing and the stated impact are both wrong, which is why I dropped severity two notches: (1) 'a fix exists and was simply not taken' is not supportable - uv.lock was last modified 2026-09-07 (git log -1 -- uv.lock), the fixed 1.15.0 was published 2026-09-09, and the Dependabot uv lane fires Mondays, i.e. 2026-09-14, the day after this snapshot; no fixed version existed when the lock was last written. (2) The exploit path is not reachable from anything this repo ships or runs: accelerate is not a declared dependency of any published opaque wheel (only transitive through peft/trl, which are dev-group and extras), transformers 5.16.1 in the lock does not even depend on accelerate, and grep over the whole tree finds zero uses of load_checkpoint_in_model / load_checkpoint_and_dispatch / dispatch_model. The only device_map= in the repo is packages/opaque-transformers/tests/validation/test_training.py:539. The finding's claim that 'exactly what examples/train_*.py do' triggers this is false - none of the eight examples/ scripts uses device_map or a sharded-index loader. The advisory itself is AV:L/UI:R: it needs an operator to point an accelerate checkpoint loader at an attacker-controlled shard index. Net effect today is dependency-scanner noise in dev/CI environments plus a one-line lock bump.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: The committed uv.lock pins accelerate 1.14.0, the last version affected by GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 (path traversal / DoS via unsanitised weight_map entries in load_checkpoint_in_model and load_checkpoint_and_dispatch). Every `uv sync --group dev --all-packages --extra all` and every CI lane therefore installs a package with a live MODERATE advisory, and any repo-wide OSV/pip-audit scan will flag it. The fixed 1.15.0 was published 2026-09-09, two days after uv.lock was last regenerated (2026-09-07), and the weekly Dependabot uv lane had not yet run, so this is a pending bump rather than an ignored fix. No Opaque code path is exploitable: accelerate is only a transitive dependency of peft/trl (dev group + extras, not a dependency of any published opaque wheel), the repo never calls load_checkpoint_in_model / load_checkpoint_and_dispatch / dispatch_model, and none of examples/train_*.py passes device_map. Remediation is `uv lock --upgrade-package accelerate`; the durable value in the finding is its secondary suggestion - the grouped `workspace-dependencies` Dependabot lane means a security bump rides with unrelated updates, and there is no OSV/pip-audit check over uv.lock or Cargo.lock in CI (I confirmed zero OSV hits across Cargo.lock's crates as well).

confirmed.title: third_party_provenance.toml misattributes riskcal to a nonexistent google-research repository, and one upstream's homepage is prose rather than a URL
confirmed.reasoning: Both defects exist in the current tree, though at different line numbers than cited (drift: riskcal homepage is /home/user/opaque/third_party_provenance.toml:105, not 126; the random-allocation homepage is :82, not 112). (1) riskcal: the file declares homepage = "https://github.com/google-research/riskcal". WebFetch of that URL returns HTTP 404. The real project is https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal (MIT, 'Measure and calibrate operational privacy risks for differentially private algorithms'), and PyPI riskcal 1.5.1 metadata gives project_urls = {'Repository': 'https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal.git'} with license MIT; a web search corroborates authorship by Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez under the interpretable-dp org, not Google Research. So the manifest credits the wrong organization and points at a dead URL. (2) The 'Random-allocation reference implementation' entry does put a prose sentence in the homepage field, verified verbatim at :82. Severity dropped from medium to low on impact, not on fact: the riskcal entry is disposition = "inspired", requires_notice = false, and riskcal appears nowhere in NOTICE (I grepped), so no published wheel or NOTICE currently misstates attribution - the error is confined to an internal inventory file. The random-allocation entry's NOTICE text (NOTICE:107-118) already identifies the upstream only by paper title and Apache-2.0 terms, the same granularity as the toml, so the toml is not degrading an existing published attribution. ARC-009 is marked Planned in .junie/architecture-contracts.md and the manifest-to-NOTICE generator does not exist yet; there is also no schema or validator anywhere in the repo that defines `homepage` as a URL (grep for third_party_provenance finds no consumers), so 'homepage must be absolute http(s)' is the auditor's reasonable convention rather than a stated contract. The riskcal wrong-URL half is a genuine one-line factual fix worth making on a public repo; the prose-homepage half is a data-quality nit.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: third_party_provenance.toml:105 attributes riskcal to https://github.com/google-research/riskcal, which does not exist (HTTP 404); the real upstream is https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal (MIT, by Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez), so a checked-in provenance file on a public repository credits the wrong organization and gives an unresolvable link. Separately, third_party_provenance.toml:82 stores a sentence ('ICML 2026 reference implementation for "Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation"') in the homepage field, so that upstream has no resolvable reference at all even though it is disposition = "adapted" with requires_notice = true. Impact today is limited to this file: riskcal has requires_notice = false and appears nowhere in NOTICE, and NOTICE's random-allocation section (NOTICE:107-118) already identifies that upstream by paper title only, so no published wheel or NOTICE text is currently wrong. The exposure is that ARC-009's planned NOTICE generator would propagate both values the moment it is built, and that anyone doing an attribution review from this file cannot reach either upstream.

confirmed.title: The repository's squash setting discards every PR body, contradicting AGENTS.md and the PR template and disabling git-cliff's BREAKING CHANGE detection
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced end to end, including the repository setting. GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque (authenticated) returns squash_merge_commit_title = "PR_TITLE", squash_merge_commit_message = "BLANK", allow_merge_commit = false, allow_rebase_merge = false; the main ruleset further restricts allowed_merge_methods to ["squash"]. AGENTS.md:64-66 says the opposite ('the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`). Both feed `git-cliff`'), and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 repeats it ('On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads'). I proved the behaviour rather than inferring it: PR #974 (Dependabot) has a multi-kilobyte body, was squash-merged on 2026-09-07, and the resulting commit 9eabd4c6 has a completely empty body - Dependabot always writes a body, so this is conclusive. Every one of the 40 most recent commits under 12146ec4 has an empty body or only Co-authored-by trailers. cliff.toml:40 does contain { body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE", group = "Breaking" } and cliff.toml:44 sets protect_breaking_commits = true, so that parser can never fire. Two corrections that pull severity down to low. First, the finding overstates the documentation spread: CONTRIBUTING.md:255-260 is actually consistent with the real setting ('the PR title is the commit message on `main`') and documents only `!` for breaking changes, so the contradiction is confined to AGENTS.md:64-66 and the PR template, not to CONTRIBUTING.md. Second, cliff.toml's sibling parser { message = ".*!:", group = "Breaking" } still works, and the team uses `!` in titles in practice (b9b0a23e fix(transformers)!:, 873de427 delete(dpsgd)!:, e8f87cd1 fix(dpsgd)!:, f2d90d61 fix(random)!:, 79acf31d fix(accounting)!:), so no release has actually lost a Breaking section - the hazard is latent, triggered only by a contributor who follows AGENTS.md's footer option instead of `!`. No code, artifact, or privacy impact; the real cost is the permanent loss of PR rationale from git log.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: The repository is configured squash_merge_commit_title = PR_TITLE, squash_merge_commit_message = BLANK (verified via the authenticated repo API), so every squash commit body is empty apart from GitHub's Co-authored-by trailers - demonstrated by Dependabot PR #974, whose long body produced an empty body on commit 9eabd4c6. AGENTS.md:64-66 and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 both tell contributors the opposite (CONTRIBUTING.md:255-260 is correct and only documents `!`). Two consequences. (a) The 'why' prose the PR template asks for never reaches git log or release notes. (b) cliff.toml:40's { body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE" } parser and protect_breaking_commits = true read the commit body and can therefore never fire, so a contributor who follows AGENTS.md:78 and declares a breaking change with only a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the PR body gets the commit grouped by its type prefix instead of under Breaking in the drafted release notes. This has not yet happened: every breaking commit in the delta range uses `!` in the title, which cliff.toml's message parser still catches. Fix is either setting squash_merge_commit_message = PR_BODY or deleting the footer option from AGENTS.md and the body parser from cliff.toml.

confirmed.title: The required status check "Qodana / Qodana" can never report on a fork pull request, so the documented external-contribution path cannot merge
confirmed.reasoning: Every link verified, including the one the finding itself only rated 'medium' confidence. Ruleset: GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/rulesets/12831618 (enforcement active, ~DEFAULT_BRANCH) requires exactly seven contexts, one of which is {"context": "Qodana / Qodana", "integration_id": 15368}; the pull_request rule requires 1 approving review and allowed_merge_methods ["squash"]; bypass_actors = [{RepositoryRole 5, always}]. Workflow: .github/workflows/pr.yml:248-272 - job `qodana`, `name: Qodana`, guarded by `if: (success() || failure()) && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, calling ./.github/workflows/qodana.yml whose jobs.scan is `name: Qodana` (qodana.yml:28-31), giving the composed context 'Qodana / Qodana'. I then proved the skip behaviour empirically instead of assuming it: in run 34686188621 (draft PR #1030, sha c4be0b93, the other branch of the same guard) the jobs API reports a single job named exactly 'Qodana' with conclusion 'skipped', and the check-runs API for c4be0b93 lists 'Qodana' skipped with no 'Qodana / Qodana' entry at all, while 'Python tests' and 'Rust tests' both report success. So when the guard is false the required context is never created, which is precisely what would happen for a non-draft fork PR, and a required context that never reports leaves the PR at 'Expected - waiting for status to be reported'. The contrast the finding draws is also real: pr.yml:186-217 ('Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules', with jq that tolerates skipped python-tests-cuda* legs) and pr.yml:231-247 (rust-test-gate) apply exactly the gate pattern that Qodana lacks. docs/development/index.md:3,9-11 and README.md:185-186 do document the fork path, and allow_forking is true. Severity cut from medium to low on impact: forks_count is 0, so no fork PR has ever been opened; the sole merger of record (evgri243, merged_by on #974) holds the admin role that the ruleset grants bypass_mode 'always'; and the guard itself is defensible because .github/workflows/ci.yml:167 shows Qodana needs secrets.QODANA_TOKEN, which GitHub withholds from fork pull_request runs, so running it unguarded on forks would fail rather than help. The residual defect is genuine but narrow: a first external contributor sees a permanently pending required check and needs an admin to bypass, and fork PRs get no static-analysis coverage.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: The active main ruleset (id 12831618) requires the context 'Qodana / Qodana', which is produced only when pr.yml's `qodana` caller job instantiates the reusable qodana.yml `scan` job. That caller is guarded by `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` (and `!draft`), and I verified on the draft branch of the same guard (run 34686188621, sha c4be0b93, PR #1030) that a skipped caller emits a check run named 'Qodana' with conclusion skipped and no 'Qodana / Qodana' check run at all. A non-draft pull request opened from a fork - the path docs/development/index.md:3,9-11 and README.md:186 tell external contributors to use, with allow_forking true - therefore has one of its seven required contexts permanently unreported ('Expected - waiting for status to be reported') and cannot be merged except by a user holding the admin role the ruleset grants bypass_mode 'always'. It also receives no Qodana coverage, though that part is partly unavoidable since ci.yml:167 shows Qodana needs secrets.QODANA_TOKEN, which fork pull_request runs do not get. No fork has actually hit this yet (forks_count = 0) and the repo's regular merger is an admin who can bypass, so the practical cost is a blocked or confusing first external PR. The fix is the gate-job pattern already used at pr.yml:186-217 ('Python tests') and pr.yml:231-247 ('Rust tests'): add an `if: always()` job named e.g. 'Qodana gate' that passes on success or skipped, and require that context instead.

confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: A first-time contributor following CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Good starting points' clicks /labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted; neither slug exists in the repository (the real labels are 'good first issue' and 'help wanted', and today both carry zero issues), so neither link surfaces a startable task. confirmed.title: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is disabled on the public repository and SECURITY.md states no concrete disclosure window
confirmed.reasoning: Both factual halves reproduced. GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting returns HTTP 200 {"enabled": false}, and the repo is public (private: false, visibility: 'public'), so the GitHub-native 'Report a vulnerability' form is indeed unavailable. SECURITY.md re-read in full (51 lines): lines 11-15 direct reporters to security@jetbrains.com with a PGP key and forbid public issues/discussions; lines 39-43 delegate handling to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy and say only 'Please allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure'. grep confirms no number of days anywhere in the file. Two corrections that materially soften the finding as written. First, the framed consequence is overstated: SECURITY.md exists at the repository root, which is exactly what GitHub renders as 'Security policy' on the Security tab and in the repo sidebar, so a researcher does see a designated private route (the mailto plus PGP key) - the missing item is the native form, not the private channel. Second, SECURITY.md:28-35 already routes non-sensitive DP/accounting defects to the public tracker and reserves the private channel for material-privacy-impact cases, so the 'no visible correct destination' framing does not hold. Delegating the timeline to a real, reachable org-level coordinated-disclosure policy is a legitimate practice, not a defect; the absence of a project-specific number of days is a completeness preference. Net: two verified configuration/policy observations, no functional or privacy impact - low.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Private vulnerability reporting is toggled off on this public repository (API: {"enabled": false}), so the Security tab shows the rendered SECURITY.md policy but no native 'Report a vulnerability' draft-advisory form. An outside researcher's private route is therefore the security@jetbrains.com mailto at SECURITY.md:11-13 (with the PGP key) - a working channel, just not the 2026-standard in-product one, and its absence also means no draft GitHub Security Advisory / CVE workflow for the published opaque-* distributions. Separately, SECURITY.md states no project-specific acknowledgement or disclosure window, deferring entirely to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy (verified reachable), so reporter and maintainer share no explicit numeric expectation. Neither item causes a wrong result or a privacy loss.

One fairness note the finding already acknowledges: .junie/architecture-contracts.md marks ARC-004, ARC-005 and ARC-011 'Planned' and instructs reviewers not to report absent planned infrastructure as a violation, so the gap is a consciously deferred one rather than an oversight. confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: No test or CI job currently asserts that opaque-accounting imports without torch, although README.md:42, AGENTS.md:32/41/130 and the installation docs advertise 'pip install opaque-accounting' as torch-free standalone. The two contract tests that enforced it were deleted in 864a6442 (#587) and the sole post-build scenario in .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml installs opaque[all], where torch is always present. A future change that adds an 'import torch' (directly or through an opaque-engine helper) under packages/opaque-accounting/src would pass every lane, and the published wheel - which declares only opaque-base - would fail to import in the environment the docs promise. The property is verified to hold at 12146ec4 (no torch import under packages/opaque-accounting), so this is a missing guard, not a break; the replacement post-build validation (ARC-004/ARC-005/ARC-011) is explicitly marked 'Planned' in .junie/architecture-contracts.md.

confirmed.title: AGENTS.md's "Accounting native module" section is factually wrong on all three of its claims and contradicts AGENTS.md's own package table
confirmed.reasoning: Verified all three statements independently in the current tree. I ran the notebook's own setup with the shipped code (torch 2.14, .venv): coin_flip(key=key(42), num_canaries=500) leaves len(train_data)=252, so sample_rate=0.25397 and the notebook's total_steps=200*(252//64)=600. With the shipped accountant, poisson eps at delta=1e-5 = 250.886 and unamplified gaussian(0.5)*600 = 1408.936 (the finding's 1408.936 matches exactly; its 253.2 came from assuming 250 train examples). I additionally found an error the finding missed and which makes it worse: with 252 examples, batch_size=64 and DataLoader's default drop_last=False the loop performs ceil(252/64)=4 releases per epoch, i.e. 800 steps, while total_steps counts 252//64=3 per epoch, i.e. 600. The conservative bound for the loop as actually written is therefore gaussian(0.5)*800 = 1841.258, a 7.3x understatement of the published 250.886. One sub-claim I could not sustain and have dropped: the finding argues the `p - (lr / bs) * g` update leaks because bs is 'a data-dependent quantity the mechanism never noised'. Under the fixed shuffled partition used here bs is deterministic per step (64,64,64,60), so it is just a per-step learning-rate scale, not a data-dependent release; that objection applies to the Poisson-sampled notebooks, not this one. Severity medium, not high: the library code is correct, this is a synthetic tutorial whose epsilon is meaninglessly large either way (250 vs 1841), and the printed 'OK' line still holds numerically because the audited epsilon is far below both bounds. (Note the finding's harness detail matters: holding the gradient fixed across trials gives a max BELOW 1.0, because the center's rounding error is then identical every draw; the excess only appears with a fresh direction per trial.) Noise cardinality also reproduced: 2945 distinct values under bf16 vs 199721 under fp32 over 200000 draws at nm=1.0. SEVERITY DROPPED from medium to low, and the 'contradiction' framing is weaker than stated: a reference table enumerating the dtypes an API accepts is not a contradiction of a guidance page that warns against using two of them - the two pages have different jobs, and precision.md (the page the docs themselves designate as owning compute_dtype) already states exactly the hazard the finding describes. The measured effect is also tiny: 1.2e-4 relative sensitivity inflation measured, and even the adversarial bound is only ~2*2^-9 ~ 0.4% of C for bf16 (the clipped sum obeys ||S|| <= max_norm, so the rounding perturbation cannot scale beyond eps*max_norm), so the epsilon understatement is sub-percent. The coarse-discretization concern is real in principle (floating-point DP, Mironov 2012) but I did not convert it into an epsilon delta, and it too requires the deliberate opt-in. Actionable residue: repeat precision.md's caveat (or link it) in the two DPTrainer tables, and emit a one-time warning from _validate_compute_dtype when compute_dtype is narrower than float32.

(the explicit guard at :1222-1228 runs first). Both messages reproduced verbatim. confirmed.title: Default-on fused-CE forward wrapper silently drops Cohere logit_scale / Granite logits_scaling / Gemma2 final_logit_softcapping on its non-fused branch
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced the numerical defect and verified every link. (1) Default-on gate: _factory.py:374-376 reads kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy') and falls back to `performance` when None; git show c0f95ced confirms the previous gate was kwargs.get('fused_linear_cross_entropy', False) plus a docstring saying it 'defaults to False'. _dp_trainer.py:844-850 always calls apply_model_patches(..., performance=True), and _dp_trainer.py:2437-2442 injects loss_only=True whenever _fused_forward_uses_marker (set at :866-875) is true. In my repro a bare apply_model_patches(m) installed the wrapper (loss_only appears in inspect.signature(m.forward).parameters) for Cohere, Granite, Gemma2 and Llama. (2) The fallback branch (cross_entropy.py:356-364) re-implements the HF tail as logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states[:, slice_indices, :]); loss = self.loss_function(logits, labels, self.vocab_size, **kwargs) with no family transform, while the fused branch threads logit_scale / logits_scaling / softcap into the kernels at :308-323. (3) The transform really lives in ForCausalLM.forward, not in loss_function: transformers 5.15.1 cohere/modeling_cohere.py:503 `logits = logits * self.logit_scale`, cohere2:481, granite/modeling_granite.py:497 `logits = logits / self.config.logits_scaling`, gemma2:527-530 softcapping tanh. Config defaults make this live: CohereConfig/Cohere2Config logit_scale=0.0625, Gemma2Config final_logit_softcapping=30.0 (GraniteConfig defaults logits_scaling=1.0, but real Granite checkpoints set it >1; Gemma3TextConfig defaults softcapping to None, so gemma3 is largely unaffected in practice). (4) Measured on CPU with tiny models, forcing the fallback by monkeypatching _fused_linear_ce_loss_is_supported to False: fused branch matches the unpatched HF loss to 0.0000% for every family, while the fallback diverges for cohere (+0.27% at random init, +53.0% with lm_head scaled 10x, +602% at 50x) and granite (-0.36% / +10.0% / +215%); llama and gemma2-at-small-logits are unaffected. The divergence grows with logit magnitude, so on a real checkpoint it is large, not marginal. I also confirmed a device-independent silent route: passing a correctly padded shift_labels (shape [B,T]) on CPU yields patched=6.37459 vs HF=4.16521 (+53.0%) with no error; passing shift_labels of shape [B,T-1] or logits_to_keep!=0 instead raises a ValueError from fixed_cross_entropy rather than corrupting. (5) No test covers the fallback: test_fused_ce_text_family_parity.py only parametrizes olmo2/olmo3/smollm3/ministral/glm4 (none of the scaled families), its scaling tests assert the fused path only ('fallback should not run'), and test_fused_ce_wrapper_preserves_logits_to_keep passes labels=None so the wrapper delegates to original() at :204-220. REACHABILITY, which is where I lower critical to high: the CUDA route is a plain boolean I could not execute (no GPU here) but is trivially readable - use_fused_ce requires (hidden_states.is_cuda and dtype in (bf16, fp16)) or not is_cuda, so CUDA + fp32 hidden states takes the fallback, and DPTrainer defaults bf16=False (_training_arguments.py:415) with _setup_precision leaving _train_dtype at whatever the caller pre-placed (_dp_trainer.py:904-905, no forcing, no warning). That combination needs fp32 model weights on CUDA: it is a documented first-class mode (docs/user-guide/precision.md '## float32 training') and an offered example flag (examples/train_dpftrl.py --dtype float32), but it is NOT what the most literal default flow produces, because transformers 5.15 from_pretrained defaults dtype='auto' (modeling_utils.py:3986, :4136-4137) and cohere/granite/gemma2 checkpoints are bf16, which routes to the correct fused branch. On CPU/MPS the fused (chunked) branch always wins, so those hosts are safe unless a caller supplies shift_labels. Impact is utility, not privacy: clipping and noise still apply to whatever gradient is produced, so epsilon is unaffected.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: DPTrainer DP-SFT of a Cohere / Cohere2 / Granite / Gemma2 checkpoint loaded in float32 on a CUDA GPU with the default bf16=False. apply_model_patches(..., performance=True) installs the fused-CE forward wrapper by default since c0f95ced (#988), the trainer sets loss_only=True, but use_fused_ce (cross_entropy.py:282-292) requires half-precision hidden states on CUDA, so fp32 hidden states fall into the else branch at :356-364, which recomputes logits = lm_head(hidden) and calls self.loss_function without the family's post-lm_head transform (Cohere logits*0.0625, Granite logits/logits_scaling, Gemma2 softcapping tanh). Every per-example loss and gradient is then computed on the wrong objective, with no exception and no warning; DP clipping and noise still apply, so the run looks healthy and epsilon is unaffected. Measured on CPU with tiny models by forcing the same branch: the fused branch matches unpatched HF exactly (0.0000%), while the fallback gives cohere +0.27% at random init, +53.0% with lm_head scaled 10x and +602% at 50x, and granite -0.36% / +10.0% / +215% - the error grows with logit magnitude, so a trained checkpoint is badly wrong, not marginally. A device-independent silent route also exists: a caller (e.g. a padding-free collator) passing shift_labels of shape [B,T] reproduces cohere +53.0% on CPU. Not reachable on CPU/MPS otherwise, and not reachable with the transformers-5 default dtype='auto' (bf16 checkpoints route to the correct fused branch), so the trigger is fp32-on-CUDA - a documented supported mode (docs/user-guide/precision.md 'float32 training', examples/train_dpftrl.py --dtype float32) rather than the most literal default. No test pins the fallback branch for any scaled family.

confirmed.title: The multi-output `apply` override added by #987 breaks `torch.func.grad` without an enclosing `vmap` for both linear-CE kernels
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced independently on the current tree with the repo venv (torch 2.14.0). packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/kernels/_linear_ce_chunked.py:277-281 overrides `apply` to return `super().apply(*args)[0]`, and :330 unpacks `_, lse, token_weight = output`. Under a bare functorch Grad transform, torch/_functorch/autograd_function.py:124-150 builds `Generated`, whose forward re-enters `custom_function_call` one level down; with no vmap level left that lands on the overridden `apply`, so `Generated.setup_context` receives a single tensor. Instrumenting `setup_context` shows it called twice: once with the real 3-tuple and once with a bare Tensor. Results: `grad(f)` and `grad(f, (0,1))` over `linear_cross_entropy_chunked` raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`; `vmap(grad(...))` and plain `.backward()` both succeed. Confirmed it is a regression: the same probe against `git show a839782e^:.../_linear_ce_chunked.py` gives `OLD grad(0) OK` and `OLD vmap(grad) OK`. Confirmed the user-facing path: `opaque.api.alignment.sft.loss._nll.fused_nll_loss` routes to the chunked kernel on CPU whenever opaque-patches is importable (packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/_fused_lce.py:40-62), and `grad(fused_nll_loss)` fails with the same ValueError while `vmap(grad(...))` and `.backward()` pass. Confirmed the consumer: packages/opaque-auditing/src/opaque/api/auditing/attacks/_gradient.py:144 is `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` with no vmap, called per example at :159, so any fused-LM-head `loss_fn` makes `gradient_scores` raise. Confirmed no test covers bare grad: packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/test_linear_ce_chunked.py and test_linear_cross_entropy.py use only `vmap(grad(...))` and `torch.autograd.grad`. One correction to the finding: the failure is not always ValueError. When the per-token loss vector has exactly 3 elements (e.g. seq_len 4), iterating the 1-D tensor satisfies the 3-way unpack with garbage and the failure moves to `TypeError: _ChunkedLinearCE.backward() missing 2 required positional arguments` — still a hard error, never a silent wrong number. The Triton twin (linear_cross_entropy.py:1005-1008 override, :1061 four-way unpack) has the identical shape and the same functorch mechanism, but it is CUDA/Triton-only so I could not execute it; that one link is inferred from code, not run.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: On the current tree, any bare `torch.func.grad` (no enclosing `vmap`) over the fused/chunked linear cross-entropy raises instead of returning a gradient. Reproduced on CPU with the repo venv: `grad(lambda h: linear_cross_entropy_chunked(h, w, labels))(h)` -> `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 3)`, and `grad(lambda h: fused_nll_loss(h, w, labels))(h)` -> the same, while `vmap(grad(...))` and `loss.backward()` both work. Pre-#987 (a839782e^) bare `grad` worked, so this is a regression introduced by the multi-output `apply` override. The concrete blast radius is `opaque.auditing.gradient_scores`, whose only differentiation path is `grad_fn = torch.func.grad(loss_fn)` (_gradient.py:144): a gradient-norm privacy audit against any model or loss that uses the fused LM-head CE cannot run at all. Failure is always loud (ValueError, or TypeError when the token count happens to be 3 and the tensor unpack accidentally succeeds); no silently wrong gradients, no epsilon impact. The DP-SGD training path (`clipped_grad` -> vmap(grad)) and ordinary `.backward()` are unaffected, which is why CI is green. The Triton CUDA twin carries the identical override and a four-way unpack and is expected to break the same way; that was not executed (no CUDA host).

confirmed.title: `_can_use_native_gqa`'s functorch guard never fires on the DP-SGD transform: `is_batchedtensor` is False under `vmap(grad(...))`
confirmed.reasoning: The predicate claim is true and I verified it directly. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:124 reads `if query.device.type != "cuda" or torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor(query): return False`. Probing the three transforms on this torch build: plain `vmap` -> is_batchedtensor True / is_gradtrackingtensor False; `vmap(grad(...))` -> is_batchedtensor **False** / is_gradtrackingtensor True; bare `grad` -> False / True. The DP path is vmap-outside-grad (packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/clipping/_clipped_grad.py uses `grad_and_value`, wrapped by `_vmap` in _clipped_fun.py), so the tensor reaching attention is grad-tracking on the outside and the single-level check misses it. The correct two-level unwrap idiom already exists in the same package (_linear_ce_chunked.py:88-103). No test asserts the negative case; test_attention.py:192-201 is CUDA-marked and uses plain tensors. HOWEVER I have to cut the claimed consequences down substantially. (a) 'SDPAParams reads wrapper geometry / wrong shapes' is refuted: constructing `torch.backends.cuda.SDPAParams` inside `vmap(grad(...))` succeeds and reports the *logical* per-example shape (probe: (2,3,4,4) plain vs (3,4,4) inside the transform), i.e. the geometry it sees is the right one. (b) 'numerics could be wrong' is refuted: `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., enable_gqa=True)` under `vmap(grad(...))` agrees bit-for-bit with the repeat_interleave reference for dQ/dK/dV (maxdiff 0.0 in float64), it just emits functorch's 'no batching rule' performance-fallback warning. (c) 'defeating #985's purpose' is unmeasured and plausibly backwards: `_grouped_sdpa` also issues its SDPA calls on the same functorch-wrapped tensors, so it takes the same fallback loop once per KV head, i.e. more fallback launches than the native call. So what remains is a genuine dead guard whose only established consequence is that the branch the author meant to exclude is taken; no correctness or privacy impact, and the perf direction is unverified (no CUDA host here).
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: On CUDA, a DP-SGD step under `vmap(grad(...))` reaches `_can_use_native_gqa` with a GradTrackingTensor, for which `torch._C._functorch.is_batchedtensor` returns False (verified on this torch build), so the guard added by #985 does not fire and the native `enable_gqa=True` SDPA branch runs inside the transform instead of `_grouped_sdpa`. Established consequence: none beyond branch selection. `SDPAParams` built from the wrapper reports the correct logical per-example geometry, and `enable_gqa=True` under `vmap(grad(...))` produces gradients identical to the explicit head-replication reference (maxdiff 0.0, float64), taking functorch's per-sample batching fallback. So this is a guard that silently does nothing on the DP transform (it still works under plain `vmap`, where is_batchedtensor is True) — a code-hygiene/perf-intent defect, not a numerical or privacy defect. Whether the native branch is faster or slower than `_grouped_sdpa` under the fallback was not measured (no CUDA device available).

confirmed.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper applies RoPE on Cohere2's NoPE (full-attention) layers
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced independently. Upstream transformers 5.15.1 .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/transformers/models/cohere2/modeling_cohere2.py:196 sets `self.sliding_window = config.sliding_window if config.layer_types[layer_idx] == 'sliding_attention' else None` and :226-228 applies rotary only `if self.sliding_window is not None` — the full-attention layers are deliberately NoPE. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:25 keeps 'Cohere2Attention' in `_FUSEABLE_QKV_ATTENTION_CLASSES`, :43-44 routes it to the generic `_make_fused_qkv_attention_forward`, and :127-133 calls `apply_rotary_pos_emb(query_states, key_states, cos, sin)` with no guard. I built a 4-layer Cohere2 with layer_types ['sliding_attention','full_attention','sliding_attention','full_attention'], installed a reference `_opaque_fused_qkv` (plain projections, the same technique tests/peft/test_gemma3_fused_lora_qkv.py:126-139 uses) and forced the CUDA branch by patching `torch.Tensor.is_cuda`: per-layer self_attn output vs the unpatched forward gives maxdiff 0.0 on both sliding layers and 1.9e-04 (1.24% rel) / 1.3e-04 (0.84% rel) on the two full-attention layers. Only the NoPE layers diverge, which isolates the cause to the unconditional rotary call. Reachability verified: `apply_model_patches` has `peft: bool = True` (packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/__init__.py:25), `_auto_fuse_lora` installs the wrapper whenever q/k/v all carry LoRA with frozen bias and no lora_dropout (peft/_router.py:74-97; PEFT's default lora_dropout is 0.0), and `_lora_patching_allowed` does not block it. The wrapper delegates to the original forward only when `not hidden_states.is_cuda` (qkv.py:106), so the bug fires exactly on the GPU training path. No sibling guard exists: transformers/models/cohere2.py installs only MLP/causal-LM patches (rms_norm_kind=None, fused_add_rms_kind=None) and never replaces Cohere2Attention.forward, so upstream's guard is live until the peft wrapper displaces it. Test-gap claim verified: Cohere2Config(num_hidden_layers=1).layer_types == ['sliding_attention'], and the only Cohere2 fused-LoRA test (tests/peft/test_fused_lora_parallel_residual.py:47-53, :127-131) uses num_hidden_layers=1, so a full-attention layer is never instantiated. Default Cohere2Config (40 layers) makes every 4th layer full_attention, so 25% of layers are affected. Severity lowered from critical to high: it is silent numerical divergence at default patch settings for a documented supported family, but it needs a specific model family plus LoRA on all of q/k/v plus CUDA, and it has no epsilon/privacy effect (affects_epsilon false).
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Load a Cohere2 model (default config: layer_types repeat 3x sliding_attention + 1x full_attention, so 10 of 40 layers are NoPE), wrap it with a LoraConfig targeting q_proj/k_proj/v_proj, call `opaque.patches.apply_model_patches(model)` (peft fusion is on by default) and train on CUDA. `_auto_fuse_lora` replaces every Cohere2Attention.forward with the generic fused wrapper, which applies `apply_rotary_pos_emb` unconditionally, whereas upstream applies it only on sliding-window layers. Every full-attention layer therefore computes attention on RoPE-rotated Q/K although the architecture defines it as NoPE: forward, loss and per-sample gradients are wrong for 25% of layers and nothing warns or raises. Verified device-independently by forcing the CUDA branch on a 4-layer Cohere2: sliding layers match upstream exactly (maxdiff 0.0) while both full-attention layers diverge (1.9e-04 / 1.3e-04 max abs, 1.24% / 0.84% relative on randomly initialised weights). CPU runs are unaffected because the wrapper delegates to the original forward when the input is not CUDA, and the only existing Cohere2 fused-LoRA test uses num_hidden_layers=1, whose single layer is sliding_attention, so no test instantiates the broken case. No privacy/epsilon impact; the defect is silent numerical infidelity to the loaded architecture.

confirmed.title: Generic fused LoRA QKV wrapper drops sliding_window and softcap, silently disabling Mistral/Gemma2 windowed attention and Gemma2 logit softcapping
confirmed.reasoning: Reproduced both halves independently on the current tree (transformers 5.15.1, torch 2.14). Code chain verified line by line: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/peft/components/qkv.py:155-164 calls attention_interface(self, q, k, v, attention_mask, dropout=..., scaling=self.scaling, **kwargs) with no sliding_window and no softcap, while upstream .venv/.../transformers/models/mistral/modeling_mistral.py:172 passes sliding_window=getattr(self.config,'sliding_window',None) and models/gemma2/modeling_gemma2.py:281-282 passes both sliding_window=self.sliding_window and softcap=self.attn_logit_softcapping. confirmed.title: Adaptive clipping releases a {0,1} clipped-count query while AdaClip accounting prices it at the {-1/2,+1/2} sensitivity, under-pricing the quantile release 2x in mu (4x in variance)
confirmed.reasoning: Both halves verified independently in the current tree. Runtime: `_clipped_fun.py:362-366` releases `num_clipped = float((norms > effective_cn).sum().item())` and `clipping_rate = num_clipped / float(batch_size)` (and :383-393 per group); `_adaptive.py:99-108` recomputes the same 0/1 count and :111-122 returns `clipping_rate + randn()*fraction_noise_std`; the per-group loops at :546-575 and :580-607 do the same with a per-group folded key; `_distributed.py` divides the global count by the realized global batch and adds the same noise. Nothing anywhere in the repo subtracts 0.5 from the indicator, and no test pins the released statistic's sensitivity against the accountant. Accountant: `adaclip.rs:30-34` returns `(1/z^2 + k/(4*sigma_b^2)).sqrt()` and `_adaclip.py:78-80` sets `sigma_b = expected_batch_size * fraction_noise_std`, so the quantile term is `k*(0.5/sigma_b)^2` - a per-record count sensitivity of 1/2 (the non-Gaussian branch at :123-126 composes `gaussian_pld(2.0*sigma_b, ...)`, same assumption). That /4 is Andrew et al.'s `z = (z_Delta^-2 + (2 z_b)^-2)^-1/2`, valid only with the +/-1/2 shift TF Privacy's quantile_estimator_query implements (`below = cast(record <= estimate) - 0.5`, GaussianSumQuery l2_norm_clip=0.5). I worked the adjacency out rather than trusting the citation: under Opaque's documented add-or-remove adjacency a {0,1} indicator sum moves by up to 1 when a record is added, so the released rate's sensitivity is <= 1/(n+1) ~ 1/W, giving mu_b = 1/sigma_b - exactly twice what the accountant charges; with the shift it would be 0.5/sigma_b and the formula would be right. Direction is anti-conservative. Reproduced the magnitude with the repo's own accountant and prebuilt Rust extension by halving fraction_noise_std (equivalent to doubling mu_b), delta=1e-5, plain Poisson: (nm=1.1, W=256, N=50000, K=1, T=1000) 0.7316 vs 0.7354 (+0.5%); (K=8) 0.7405 vs 0.7718 (+4.2%); (nm=0.8, W=64, N=50000, K=4, T=2000) 0.5791 vs 0.8467 (+46%); (nm=0.8, W=32, N=20000, K=8, T=1000) 1.3536 vs 5.3562 (3.96x); (nm=0.6, W=32, N=20000, K=16, T=1000) 4.6988 vs 16.1743 (3.44x) - the reporter's figures reproduce exactly. Reachability: _dp_trainer.py:4471-4480 wires `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(gaussian(nm), expected_batch_size=..., num_groups=...)` whenever `clipping_mode == 'adaptive'`, and `_CLIPPING_KWARGS['adaptive'] = {'target_quantile','clipping_norm_max'}` (_training_arguments.py:213-217) so `fraction_noise_std` is the shared 0.05 default on both sides; the library recipe in docs/user-guide/clipping.md:230-249 and :481-495 is the same pairing, and neither the docs nor the accountant docstring mentions any 1/2 shift. Refutation attempts that failed: no compensating factor (noise is applied to the rate, so absolute count noise is exactly batch_size*fraction_noise_std, matching the accountant's sigma_b definition); test_adaptive.py:349-356 only checks the clipped-fraction convention, not sensitivity. Not tracked as open: the nearest issue #345 'Bind AdaClip released statistic to the parameters the accountant charges' is in the 2026-08-27 open snapshot but absent from both 2026-09-13 open lists, and an earlier pass in this audit recorded it closed as not_planned. Severity high rather than critical: `clipping_mode` defaults to 'fixed' (_training_arguments.py:560) so adaptive clipping is opt-in, and the epsilon error is only ~0.5% for a single group at a large batch; 3-4x needs many per-group quantile releases at small batches.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Any run that pairs `adaptive_clipped_grad` with `dpsgd_acc.adaclip(...)` - including DPTrainer with `clipping_mode='adaptive'`, which wires that pairing itself at the shared default fraction_noise_std=0.05. The runtime releases `num_clipped/batch_size + N(0, 0.05^2)` from a 0/1 clipping indicator (per-record sensitivity ~1/W), while the accountant prices the release at sensitivity 1/(2W) (`k/(4*sigma_b^2)` in adaclip.rs:33 with sigma_b = expected_batch_size*0.05). The quantile term's mu is understated by exactly 2x (4x in variance) and the reported epsilon is not an upper bound. Measured with the repo's accountant at delta=1e-5: single-group default (nm=1.1, W=256, N=50000, T=1000) reports 0.7316 against a correctly-priced 0.7354 (0.5% low); per-group configurations - documented and supported at docs/user-guide/clipping.md:481-495 - are much worse because num_groups multiplies the mispriced term: K=8 at W=32, nm=0.8, T=1000 reports 1.3536 against 5.3562 (3.96x low), K=16 at nm=0.6 reports 4.6988 against 16.1743 (3.44x low). confirmed.title: Resuming a DDP run restores rank 0's sampler key on every rank, so all ranks draw the same local indices and Poisson/b-min-sep/BnB amplification loses its independent-inclusion hypothesis

Same absolute-key restore spot-checked in dpftrl/_poisson.py:304, _b_min_sep.py:259, _balls_in_bins.py:260. Reproduced: `PoissonSampler(range(1000), 0.05, key=fold_in(key(7), r))` gives different first batches for r=0/1 ([19,29,42,...] vs [39,55,60,...]); after `from_state_dict(template_r, state_dict(rank0_sampler))` both ranks hold RngKey(seed=12201757873983228112, impl='opaque_threefry_like') and emit the byte-identical batch [20,43,76,86,160,197,215,224] - the reporter's exact batch. The accounting claim is the substantive part and it holds. Post-resume the mechanism is Poisson(q) over local *positions*, each carrying the W co-indexed records (shards are equal length because the dataset is trimmed to a multiple of world_size, :3886-3908), while the accountant models i.i.d. Bernoulli(q) over the global dataset (`sample_rate = expected_batch_size / effective_dataset_size`, :1490-1503). For a target x at position p the W-1 co-indexed records are in the batch iff x is, so x's indicator is not independent of the rest of the batch and the Poisson mixture no longer decomposes as (1-q)P + q(P shifted). confirmed.title: DDP resume installs rank 0's sampler snapshot on every rank, silently re-correlating the per-rank Poisson masks that the per-rank key fold exists to keep independent
