(1) Real 2-rank Gloo DDP run (packages/opaque-transformers/tests/distributed/_ddp_runner.py fixtures, world_size=2, save_steps=2, resume from checkpoint-2, use_cpu): fresh-phase stream keys are per-rank distinct (rank0 seed 1950457451192556855, rank1 seed 16528425509808239245); after resume BOTH ranks report 1950457451192556855. Rank 0's key is installed on every rank, exactly as the in-code caveat says. (2) Code path verified: the per-rank fold is `sampler_key = fold_in(sampler_key, self._ddp.rank)` guarded by `if self._ddp.world_size > 1` (_dp_trainer.py:3944-3949); the snapshot is written only under `if _distributed.should_save(a, self._ddp):` (:5151, calling `_save_dp_runtime` at :5197) and `should_save` returns `ddp.is_world_zero` by default (_distributed.py:211-222); the restore `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` (:1874-1876) is guarded only by `resume_path is not None and saved_sampler_state is not None and not a.ignore_data_skip` - no rank branch. `local_shard` gives contiguous disjoint shards (_shard.py:20-35), so 'same local index' is a fixed group of world_size records. (3) I also refuted the in-code justification at :3872-3874 ('the per-record marginal stays Bernoulli(q) either way, so the privacy accounting is unaffected') numerically. Under the shared mask the mechanism Poisson-samples GROUPS of W co-indexed records, so for neighbouring D / D u {x} the conditional pair is (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(a,s) vs (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(a+1,s) with a = (W-1) worst-case aligned clipped gradients (units of C/B, s = noise_multiplier), instead of the amplified pair N(0,s) vs (1-q)N(0,s)+qN(1,s). Numerically integrating both hockey-stick divergences: at noise_multiplier=1.0, q=0.01, world_size=4, eps=1 the executed mechanism's per-step delta is 1.26e-3 while the amplified mechanism the accountant prices gives 2.73e-9 (ratio 4.6e5); at nm=1.0, q=0.1, W=4, eps=1 it is 1.27e-2 vs 2.07e-4; at nm=2.0, q=0.1, W=8, eps=1 it is 6.8e-4 vs 1.1e-10. In the well-separated regime the executed delta converges to exactly q * delta_Gaussian(unamplified) - subsampling buys only the factor q, not the subsampled-Gaussian bound. Amplification requires the target record's inclusion indicator to be independent of the rest of the sample, which the shared mask destroys; a Bernoulli(q) marginal is not sufficient. Raised from medium to high: default `ignore_data_skip=False`, default `save_on_each_node=False`, ordinary DDP + resume, no warning, fail-open, and the source comment asserts the opposite. Not in milestones-open.tsv or other-open-issues.tsv (the FSDP2 issues #55-58 are a different subject), so the in-code 'tracked for the multi-GPU work' is not backed by an open issue I can find.
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: Any DPTrainer DDP run (world_size > 1, default save_on_each_node=False, default ignore_data_skip=False) with per-record Bernoulli sampling (poisson or cyclic_poisson) that is resumed from a checkpoint. Measured on a real 2-rank Gloo run: the fresh phase gives each rank a distinct sampler stream key (fold_in(seed, rank)), but after `resume_from_checkpoint` every rank restores the rank-0 snapshot's key_seed, so all ranks draw the identical Bernoulli(q) mask over their own disjoint contiguous shard and the world_size records sharing a local index are included or excluded together for every post-resume step. The accountant keeps charging the i.i.d.-Poisson-amplified per-step PLD. Quantified by numerically integrating the hockey-stick divergence of the group-sampled mechanism against the amplified one, with worst-case aligned co-indexed gradients: at noise_multiplier=1.0, q=0.01, world_size=4 the real per-step delta at eps=1 is 1.26e-3 versus the charged 2.73e-9; at q=0.1 it is 1.27e-2 versus 2.07e-4. No warning is emitted at resume, no distributed-lane test covers the sampler snapshot, and the source comment at _dp_trainer.py:3872-3874 asserts the accounting is unaffected, which the above refutes. The privacy exposure appears only if the reader then fixes the sampler to the conditional rate (to recover the intended batch size) while leaving the global rate in the accountant: nothing validates the pairing, since q_global < q_conditional always passes the (0,1] check. confirmed.title: calibrate()'s runtime-unsafe fallback drops the adaptive-probe union bound but still reports the undivided mc_failure_probability
confirmed.reasoning: Code path verified in packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/calibration.py: line 303 probe_count = max_iterations + 2; 304-309 probe_config divides mc_failure_probability by probe_count; 310-317 the primary search runs under probe_config; 320-330 the calibrated parameter is re-evaluated once, non-adaptively, under overall_config (this single evaluation is what legitimises reporting the undivided value on the primary path); 331-341 when runtime_safe is False the ENTIRE binary search is re-run by _calibrate_impl while still inside `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`, so every probe of that second search consumes the full mc_failure_probability, and `achieved = result.achieved` takes the reported value straight from an adaptively selected probe of that search with no non-adaptive re-evaluation; line 353 then sets result.mc_failure_probability = overall_config.mc_failure_probability. That contradicts the documented contract at calibration.py:79-81 ('Overall failure probability covering every adaptive Monte Carlo probe'). REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY TWICE by wrapping _calibrate_impl: (a) mc_resolution=1e-2, balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy()), num_bins=5, n_steps=20), epsilon_budget(8.0, 1e-5), param range 0.5-8.0 -> invocations=2, second invocation at mc_failure_probability=1e-06 with 19 iterations, reported mc_failure_probability=1e-06; (b) the SAME call at the library's true defaults (mc_resolution=1e-5, mc_failure_probability=1e-6, 2,940,252 MC samples) -> invocations=2 again, second search at 1e-06 with 19 iterations, reported 1e-06. So the fallback is reachable with default discretization and default tolerance, not only in a corner case. (A smaller case, num_bins=2/n_steps=4 at defaults, did NOT trigger it - invocations=1 - so it is config-dependent, not universal.) MAGNITUDE, which the finding overstates: the honest union over ~21 probes is ~2.1e-5 rather than 1e-6, i.e. the reported confidence is optimistic by ~21x in a quantity of order 1e-5. Because resolved_num_mc_samples is itself derived from mc_failure_probability, re-evaluating the same converged process at 1e-6/22 vs 1e-6 vs 2.2e-5 gave epsilon 7.98944 / 7.99999 / 8.01978 - under 0.3% spread - and at default mc_resolution the value was insensitive. So the defect is a mislabelled confidence field, not a materially understated epsilon. Existing tests do not catch it: test_calibration_reports_one_overall_mc_confidence_budget (packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_b_min_sep.py:229) asserts exactly the reported-equals-configured behaviour, and test_recalibrates_when_runtime_evaluation_is_unsafe (packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/accounting/test_calibration.py:608) only pins that the fallback produces a safe `achieved`. No open tracked issue covers this (#911 is about MC calibration performance).
confirmed.corrected_failure_scenario: With default discretization (mc_resolution=1e-5, mc_failure_probability=1e-6) a user calls cal.calibrate(cal.epsilon_budget(8.0, delta=1e-5), lambda nm: balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, blt_strategy()), num_bins=5, n_steps=20), 0.5, 8.0). The probe-config search converges, the single runtime re-evaluation at that parameter lands above the budget, so runtime_safe is False and calibrate() re-runs the whole binary search inside `with _use_discretization(overall_config)`: 19 iterations / ~21 Monte Carlo probes, each consuming the undivided 1e-6 rather than 1e-6/102, and the returned `achieved` is taken from one adaptively selected probe of that search. CalibrateResult.mc_failure_probability is nevertheless reported as 1e-06 (mc_confidence 0.999999), although the simultaneous coverage of those probes is only about 1-2.1e-5 - a failure mass larger than the delta=1e-5 the user calibrated at. Measured impact on the number itself is small: correcting the per-probe bound to 1e-6/22 changes the achieved epsilon by under 0.3% (7.98944 vs 7.99999 at mc_resolution=1e-2) and was not measurable at default mc_resolution. So the concrete defect is a documented confidence field that is optimistic by roughly the probe count on a path reachable at defaults, not a materially wrong epsilon.

tracked.title: IdentityStrategy.sensitivity ignores the participation schema, so bare mf_gaussian under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k)
tracked.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree. packages/opaque-dpftrl/src/opaque/api/dpftrl/noise/_identity.py:45-46 is still `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float: return 1.0`, and _mf_gaussian.py:132-141 feeds exactly that value to _native.mf_gaussian_pld as the sensitivity of the whole bare release. Measured with `uv run python`: identity_strategy().sensitivity(n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5) = 1.0 (identical to the k=1 value), while every sibling scales: band_mf 1.00000->2.23607, bsr 1.16046->2.59486, lambda_cgd 1.00000->2.23607, bisr 1.00000->2.69449, blt 1.80457->4.64553. fa.mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 4.37717809602987; the correct value for a C=I release with 5 participations (sensitivity sqrt(5), equivalently 5-fold Gaussian self-composition) is da.gaussian(1/sqrt(5)).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 11.480022787731485. The math is unambiguous: for C=I the schema sensitivity max_pi ||sum_{j in pi} e_j|| = sqrt(k), which is also just Gaussian composition. I independently checked every escape hatch and they hold: the Poisson amplifier takes the IdentityStrategy branch and sets effective_nm = noise_multiplier directly with num_groups = n_steps self-composition (_poisson.py:188-190); b_min_sep asks explicitly for min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 (_b_min_sep/__init__.py:166-169), the correct kappa=1 for identity; _balls_in_bins.py never calls sensitivity; _second_moment.py:140-145 also asks for k=1. So the defect is confined to the bare (unamplified) MfGaussian.pld path with IdentityStrategy. No test pins the buggy value: packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_identity_mf.py only exercises n_steps=1 plus explicit self-composition (lines 44-71). Mitigation, not refutation: docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 do warn 'Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation'. But the API fails open - it accepts min_sep/max_participations, ignores them, and returns a number - and the surrounding guidance in the same doc section ('For bare accounting, declare the full horizon') invites exactly the call that goes wrong. Not critical: the sanctioned DP-SGD-via-MF paths (n_steps=1 then *T, or a poisson/b_min_sep/balls_in_bins wrapper) are correct. ALREADY TRACKED: open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments consistently', state=open, labels bug/blocked/needs-design/severity: high/impact: epsilon) has as its first acceptance criterion 'Charged privacy cost is non-decreasing in max_participations for every strategy' and as its proposed direction 'Define whether strategy sensitivity is single-participation or participation-aware, then make all callers explicit'. e44d6ab6 (#998) satisfied that for BandMF only; IdentityStrategy is the residual of the same open issue, not a new defect.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: Only the bare, unamplified MF accounting path is affected: `opaque.dpftrl.accounting.mf_gaussian(sigma, identity_strategy(), n_steps=N, ...)` with N > 1. IdentityStrategy.sensitivity accepts and discards min_sep/max_participations and always returns 1.0, so MfGaussian.pld prices the release as a single sensitivity-1 Gaussian regardless of the declared schema. Measured on 12146ec4: mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=5).epsilon_at(1e-5) = 4.3772, while the correct value at sensitivity sqrt(5) is 11.4800 - a 2.62x silent under-report in the unsafe direction. The gap grows as sqrt(k); the default schema (min_sep=1, max_participations=None -> n_steps) declares k = n_steps, so the same call without explicit schema args returns the identical 4.3772 for what is really a sqrt(1000)-sensitivity release. No warning or exception is raised. All five sibling strategies (band_mf, blt, bsr, bisr, lambda_cgd) scale correctly at the same point; identity is the sole outlier. Amplified accounting (poisson, b_min_sep, balls_in_bins), the paired second-moment allocator, and the sanctioned n_steps=1 + self-compose pattern are all unaffected - each either bypasses identity sensitivity or explicitly requests the k=1 value. A documented caveat at docs/reference/accounting.md:420 and docs/user-guide/accounting.md:280 tells users not to make this call, but the API fails open rather than refusing.

tracked.title: RMSNorm / fused-add-RMSNorm / RoPE backwards overwrite the upstream gradient buffer on a single backward, not only on a repeated one (wider than tracked #898)
tracked.reasoning: The static aliasing is exactly as described and I re-read every cited line: rms_norm.py:533 `dY = dY.contiguous().view(-1, dim)` then :557 `dX = dY if in_place else torch.zeros_like(dY)`, with dX handed to the kernel as the output pointer (:562-565); fused_add_rms_norm.py:322 the same with `torch.empty_like`; rope_embedding.py:236-238 and :262-266 pass `dQ` as both in and out pointer, and :455-458 likewise for dQ_out/dK_out, with no `in_place` flag at all. `Opaque_RMSNorm.backward` (rms_norm.py:740-742) does `go = grad_output.contiguous()` then `go2 = go.reshape(-1, dim)`, so for an already-contiguous incoming grad `go2` shares storage with the engine-supplied gradient. components/rms_norm.py:35,41 do pass `in_place_bwd=True` for the default llama and gemma RMSNorm patches (gemma2/olmo2/glm4 variants pass False), and the public `opaque_rms_norm` defaults to `in_place_backward=False`. I verified the autograd-engine link with a CPU stand-in Function whose backward writes into its `grad_output`: after `torch.autograd.grad(y, x, grad_outputs=g)` the caller's `g` is observably mutated (3.0 -> 6.0), and in a shared-grad topology (`out = a + F.apply(a)`, where AddBackward hands the *same* tensor to both edges) the sibling branch's gradient comes out wrong (4.0 instead of 3.0). What I could NOT establish: (1) the Triton kernels are CUDA-only and this host has no CUDA, so the actual buffer overwrite was not executed; (2) I looked for an in-model topology among the affected families that would hit the shared-grad case and did not find one — Llama/Gemma use these norms as pre-norms whose incoming gradient is freshly allocated by the consumer projections (or accumulated across q/k/v and gate/up), and the families with a post-attention norm before the residual add (Gemma2, OLMo2, GLM4, Cohere2) are the ones configured with `in_place_bwd=False`. So the harm needs direct kernel use with an explicit `grad_outputs` that the caller then reuses, on CUDA. Tracking: this duplicates open issue #898, whose scope is recorded in this repo's own audit notes as 'the wider sweep across the other fused kernels (rope_embedding, rms_norm, fused_add_rms_norm, moe, Opaque_LoRA_QKV, Opaque_LoRA_W)' for exactly this backward-buffer-overwrite class; the first-vs-repeated distinction is a refinement to add to #898, not a separate defect.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: On CUDA with the Triton kernels, `Opaque_RMSNorm.backward` with `in_place_bwd=True` (the default for the llama and gemma RMSNorm component patches) passes the engine-supplied gradient tensor to the Triton kernel as both input and output pointer, and `_RoPEBackward` / `_RoPE_QK_Backward` do the same unconditionally. If such a node is the first node the autograd engine visits for a user-supplied `grad_outputs` — i.e. direct kernel use such as `torch.autograd.grad(opaque_rms_norm(x, w), x, grad_outputs=g)` — the caller's `g` is overwritten in place; the write goes through Triton so no version counter is bumped and autograd raises nothing. Verified on CPU with an equivalent stand-in Function that the engine does hand the caller's tensor through and that it is observably mutated, and that a shared-grad topology yields a wrong sibling gradient; the Triton overwrite itself was not executed (no CUDA host). I found no path inside the supported patched model families that reaches the shared/aliased-gradient case, because the families whose decoder layer puts a norm directly under the residual add are configured with `in_place_bwd=False`. So the practical exposure is direct kernel callers on CUDA that reuse their seed gradient, not DPTrainer or `clipped_grad` (scalar loss -> engine-created ones tensor). Same defect class as open issue #898.

tracked.title: Paired second-moment accounting is documented as unconditionally equal to the first-moment mechanism, but the runtime sizes both streams from single-participation column norms
tracked.reasoning: The defect is real and larger than claimed, but its specific criterion and magnitude are wrong, and the code half is already tracked. Verified: (1) docs/reference/accounting.md:330-338 asserts 'privacy accounting is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism' with no condition, docs/reference/noise.md:83-90 and docs/user-guide/dp-ftrl.md:176-178 repeat it, and the derivation there is stated in terms of the single-participation column norms (Delta1 = zeta*||C1||, Delta2 = zeta^2*||C2||). (2) The Mahalanobis identity itself holds exactly: paired_noise_stddevs(1.3, first=0.7, second=0.49) gives sum (Delta/sigma)^2 = 0.5917159763313609 = 1/nm^2 to the last bit. (3) _second_moment.py:138-149 computes c1 and c2 at `min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1` (single participation) and passes `noise_multiplier/c1`; confirmed at runtime that the paired first-stream base sigma is exactly sqrt(2) x the single-stream sigma when D1=D2. (4) Nothing validates the pairing: `mf_gaussian_noise(params, lambda_cgd_strategy(0.9), second_moment_strategy=lambda_cgd_strategy(0.999), n_steps=1000, min_sep=100, max_participations=10, noise_multiplier=1.0, key=key(0))` constructs and runs with zero warnings, and the only invariant test (tests/noise/test_second_moment_noise.py:194-234) pins the identity solely at min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1 - the case where the code is correct. WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG: its exhibited pair proves nothing. The DP-FTRL poisson and b_min_sep accountants both normalize by the SINGLE-participation sensitivity (_poisson.py:181-185 and _b_min_sep/__init__.py:166-171 call sensitivity(min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) and price repeats by composition/transcript DP), so band_mf pairs raise no rho mismatch there at all, and BandMfStrategy has no gram_matrix (balls_in_bins refuses it). Its rho values come from `sensitivity()`, which for BISR is a conservative majorization: bisr(bandwidth=4).sensitivity(n=1000, min_sep=100, max_part=10) = 3.8106 but its actual BnB Gram diagonal is exactly 10.0, i.e. a true blow-up of sqrt(10) = 3.1623, identical to band_mf(10)'s - so the claimed '~11% higher realized sensitivity' is an artifact of a conservative bound, not an excess. The real criterion for the BnB-accounted families is dominance of the normalized Gram, and the real magnitude is much worse. Derived and numerically validated: the paired release's BnB dominating pair has Gram [D1*G1/c1^2 + D2*G2/c2^2]*c1^2/(D1+D2) while balls_in_bins prices G1; with clipping_norm=1.0 the clipper emits max_norm=C/B and squared_max_norm=C^2/B (clipping/_clipped_fun.py:391-393), so D1=D2 and the realized Gram is (G1+G2)/2. My harness reproduces the public accounted value exactly (14.9990 = balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(1.0, lambda_cgd(0.9)), num_bins=100, n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(1e-5)), and the realized epsilon for the same release paired with lambda_cgd(0.99) is 21.01 (+40%) and with lambda_cgd(0.999) is 40.47 (+170%). That pairing mirrors the pattern the docs themselves recommend (user-guide/optimizers.md:245-247 and user-guide/noise.md:282-284 pair momentum 0.9 for the first moment with 0.999 for the second, and noise.md:305 says the squared-gradient workload 'can differ'), and lambda-cgd.md:71 tells lambdaCGD users to pass second_moment_strategy explicitly without saying which. ALREADY TRACKED: open issue #359 ('Define BandMF participation sensitivity and price second moments consistently', severity high, blocked/needs-design) states the same defect in its problem statement - 'Paired second-moment allocation also mixes single- and multi-participation sensitivities' - with the acceptance criterion 'Runtime first/second-moment allocation and accounting use the same deployed sensitivities'. The only delta is that the reference docs now assert the equality as settled; that is a documentation overstatement on top of #359, not a new defect. Severity high (matching #359) rather than medium: the epsilon understatement is silent and large, but it needs an explicitly-passed, mismatched second_moment_strategy, so not critical.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: With DP-FTRL private second moments, `mf_gaussian_noise` sizes both streams from single-participation column norms (c1, c2 computed at min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) while the balls-in-bins accountant prices the first stream through its multi-participation Gram. The documented accounting recipe (balls_in_bins(mf_gaussian(nm, first_strategy), ...), with the reference docs stating accounting 'is exactly the underlying first-moment mechanism') is then exact only when the two strategies have the same normalized Gram - which holds trivially when they are identical, and nothing checks it. Established at n_steps=1000, num_bins=100 (10 epochs), clipping_norm=1.0, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5: first=lambda_cgd(0.9) reports eps = 14.999, while the realized paired release has eps = 21.01 with second=lambda_cgd(0.99) (+40%) and eps = 40.47 with second=lambda_cgd(0.999) (+170%). The mismatched pairing is accepted with no warning, and the only regression test for the joint-budget identity covers just max_participations=1. The finding's own example (band_mf(10) + bisr(4), '~11%') does not reproduce: band_mf is accounted by poisson/b_min_sep, which normalize at single participation, and bisr(4)'s true blow-up equals band_mf(10)'s - its sensitivity() value of 3.81 is a conservative bound. The code defect is the one already tracked as open issue #359; the new element is only that docs/reference/accounting.md:336-338 and docs/reference/noise.md:85-90 now present the equality as unconditional.

tracked.title: Patching gpt_oss / deepseek_v4 silently deletes the attention sink and freezes the `sinks` parameter
tracked.reasoning: Independently reproduced on transformers 5.15.1. Chain verified link by link: (1) make_apply_family_patches defaults eager_attention_replacement=vmap_eager_attention_forward (packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/_family.py:126) and rebinds mod.eager_attention_forward when the `eager_attention` concern is on (_family.py:212-216); (2) that concern defaults from `compat`, which defaults True (_factory.py:241-247 doc + apply() signature), so it needs no opt-in; (3) models/gpt_oss.py:16-19 passes no override, models/deepseek_v4.py:16-20 overrides only rope_replacement=None; (4) vmap_eager_attention_forward (components/attention.py:365-387) ends in **kwargs and delegates to _grouped_eager_attention, a plain softmax with no sink term -- `grep -rn 'sinks|s_aux' packages/opaque-patches/src/` returns zero hits; (5) upstream GptOssAttention.forward passes `s_aux=self.sinks` into the resolved attention interface and its eager_attention_forward concatenates the sink logit before the softmax (inspected the installed source); DeepseekV4 eager_attention_forward likewise contains sinks; both families have _supports_sdpa=False, so eager is the only non-flash path. (6) Reproduction with DEFAULT kwargs: tiny GptOssForCausalLM, config._attn_implementation resolves to 'eager'; after apply_model_patches(m2) the module global is vmap_eager_attention_forward, max abs logit diff vs the unpatched model is 1.545e-01, and after a backward pass model.layers[0].self_attn.sinks.grad is None. Same script for a tiny DeepseekV4ForCausalLM: max abs logit diff 1.065e-01, model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks.grad is None. No warning is emitted, and `grep -rn -i sink docs/` returns nothing. The doc contradiction is real: docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218 says that for GPT-OSS and DeepSeek-V4 'only RMSNorm, RoPE (where standard), and cross-entropy are patched'. Two corrections to the finding. (a) Already tracked: open issue #813 ('Convert parity skips to strict xfail and resolve the gpt2 gradient mismatch', parent #769) explicitly scopes 'The remaining three exemptions are each justified in the reason string or removed', and its open closing PR #1032 names this exact defect verbatim -- the new xfail reason for both families is 'the required eager-attention compatibility shim omits the upstream self-attention sink gradient'. So the sink gap is known and in flight; the only genuinely new delta is the model-patches.md:215-218 claim and the absence of any user-facing warning. (b) The first fix option is wrong: passing eager_attention_replacement=None (the gpt2 treatment) would leave upstream's hardcoded 4-D eager attention in place (reshape(1,-1,1,1).expand(query.shape[0],...), transpose(1,2)), which is exactly what breaks under vmap -- hence 'the required ... compatibility shim'. Only the sink-aware vmap shim (forwarding s_aux into the softmax) is a real fix. Severity lowered from high to medium: no privacy effect (clipping still bounds per-record sensitivity and accounting is untouched), it is confined to two opt-in model families, the gap is acknowledged in-repo in the parity skip comments and in the in-flight PR, and the trained model is degraded rather than silently wrong in an unbounded way -- but it is silent at defaults and contradicted by the docs table, which keeps it above low.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: Fine-tuning a GPT-OSS or DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint through DPTrainer or any apply_model_patches(model) flow with DEFAULT kwargs (compat=True -> eager_attention on) rebinds transformers.models.{gpt_oss,deepseek_v4}.modeling_*.eager_attention_forward to opaque's vmap_eager_attention_forward, which swallows the s_aux kwarg and omits the attention-sink logit from the softmax. Reproduced on transformers 5.15.1 with tiny configs: forward logits shift by 1.54e-01 (gpt_oss) / 1.07e-01 (deepseek_v4) max abs versus the unpatched model, and after a backward pass model.layers.0.self_attn.sinks.grad is None, so the sink parameter never trains. No warning is emitted. Both families are exempted from forward parity (_STRICT_FORWARD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES) and gradient parity (_GRAD_PARITY_SKIP_FAMILIES) in packages/opaque-patches/tests/transformers/models/test_parity.py:87-103, so CI cannot flag it. Privacy accounting is unaffected; the defect is model fidelity, and it is contradicted by docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:215-218. The sink-gradient half is already named in open issue #813 and its closing PR #1032; the doc claim and the missing warning are not.

tracked.title: Grad-parity harness is non-deterministic under dropout and mis-attributes the failure to the patches
tracked.reasoning: Reproduced end to end with .venv (transformers 5.15.1, torch 2.14.0). get_tiny_config_kwargs() (_test_utils.py:14-27) sets no dropout keys and _base_config_kwargs('gpt2') (test_parity.py:157-168) only pops num_key_value_heads/rope_theta, so GPT2Config keeps resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1 (verified by constructing the tiny config). assert_parity_grad (:450-502) and assert_parity_vmap_grad (:517-563) both put reference and patched model into .train() and run them back to back with no reseed. Running the helpers directly: dropout 0.1 -> assert_parity_grad FAILS 'backward grad transformer.h.0.attn.c_attn.bias mismatch: abs_err=1.93e-02, rel_err=5.30e+01' and assert_parity_vmap_grad FAILS abs_err=1.12e-02; dropout 0.0 -> both PASS and 0 of 16 gradients differ under torch.equal (bit-exact), losses identical. So the skip reason 'kv_cache/batchify patches alter backward graph' (test_parity.py:97-99) is wrong and gpt2's backward is bit-exact. CORRECTION to the stated mechanism: it is not two different dropout masks off a shared RNG. The patched model has dropout deliberately zeroed by the `dropout` compat patch (_router.py:161-168 -> components/dropout.py disable_dropout), default-on whenever compat=True. Measured: patched model in .train() returns the same loss (4.912911415) on three consecutive draws and in .eval(), while the unpatched reference varies (4.910572052 / 4.887429237 / 4.908598423). The comparison is stochastic-vs-deterministic, so a reseed alone would NOT fix it; only equalizing the dropout rate does. The forward-looking claim checks out: enumerating every registered family's config defaults shows gpt2 is the only one with a nonzero default dropout rate. Already tracked: open issue #813 'Convert parity skips to strict xfail and resolve the gpt2 gradient mismatch' owns this, and its open PR #1032 applies exactly this fix (adds attn_pdrop=embd_pdrop=resid_pdrop=0.0 to _base_config_kwargs for gpt2, drops gpt2 from the grad exemptions) with a body stating the dropout root cause. Severity lowered medium->low: test-harness artifact, no user-facing behavior change, one family, already remediated in an open PR.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: On the current tree, assert_parity_grad / assert_parity_vmap_grad on GPT2LMHeadModel with the suite's tiny config (which leaves GPT-2's default resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1) compare a stochastic-dropout unpatched reference against a patched model whose dropout the `dropout` compat patch has zeroed, so all 16 parameter gradients and the loss differ (c_attn.bias abs_err=1.93e-02 backward, 1.12e-02 vmap). Setting the three rates to 0.0 makes the gradients bit-identical (0/16 differ under torch.equal) and both helpers pass, proving gpt2's backward path is exact and the recorded skip reason mis-attributes the failure. Impact is test-integrity only: one registered family was written off as having broken gradients when it is bit-exact, and any future family with a nonzero default dropout rate would false-fail the same way (gpt2 is the only such family today). Note the finding's alternative fix of reseeding between the two runs would not work, because the patched model has no dropout at all.

tracked.title: IdentityStrategy.sensitivity ignores the participation schema: bare MF accounting under-reports epsilon by sqrt(k) (145x at the default horizon)
tracked.reasoning: Reproduced end to end on the current tree. _identity.py:45-46 is verbatim `def sensitivity(self, **_) -> float: return 1.0`; _mf_gaussian.py:132-140 calls strategy.sensitivity(n_steps, min_sep, _effective_max_participations) and feeds the result to _native.mf_gaussian_pld as a participation-aware sensitivity; _mf_gaussian.py:89-95 resolves max_participations=None to _bare_n_steps. Measured: mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000).epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 4.37718, while the mechanism it models (iid Gaussian at sigma=nm*max_norm on each of 1000 steps, record present in every step) has eps = 633.930 by (dpsgd.gaussian(1.0)*1000) and 633.983 as a single Gaussian at nm/sqrt(1000) -- a 145x under-report. Flatness reproduced: at n_steps=32, min_sep=4, nm=1.0, delta=1e-5 identity gives 4.3772 for max_participations = 1/2/4/8 while band_mf_strategy(bands=8) rises 4.3772/7.8394/12.9407/20.8267 (the finding quoted 1.9931/3.4796/5.5729/8.6536, i.e. a different unstated nm or delta -- the monotonicity contrast is what reproduces, not those absolute numbers). The math is right: for C=I the k-participation schema sensitivity is sqrt(k), so the charge is short by exactly sqrt(k). No runtime guard, warning, or rejection exists; no test pins the correct behaviour (every bare-identity test in packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/accounting/test_identity_mf.py uses n_steps=1 and self-composes). Mitigations found, which the finding partly acknowledges: docs/reference/accounting.md:420-421 explicitly warns 'Bare BandMF and Identity sensitivity currently accounts for one participation. Do not use bare calls with these strategies to budget repeated participation', and noise/types.py:48-59 documents the 1.0 return. So it is a documented limitation rather than a wholly silent one -- but the same page at :405-407 tells the user max_participations defaults to n_steps and 'do not compose it again by the number of rounds', which is the contradicting instruction that makes the default bare call wrong. This is precisely acceptance criterion 1 of OPEN issue #359 ('Charged privacy cost is non-decreasing in max_participations for every strategy'), whose Problem statement is the same defect in the sibling BandMF class; #998 fixed BandMF and left Identity. Severity kept at high (matching #359's own 'severity: high' label): epsilon-losing direction, privacy-material parameter silently discarded on a public API, magnitude growing as sqrt(n_steps).
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: On commit 12146ec4, a bare-accounting call `mf_gaussian(1.0, identity_strategy(), n_steps=1000)` (max_participations left at its default, which _effective_max_participations resolves to 1000) returns epsilon 4.3772 at delta=1e-5. The mechanism it models -- mf_gaussian_noise with identity_strategy(), i.e. independent Gaussian noise at sigma = nm*max_norm on each of 1000 steps with the record present at every step -- has true epsilon 633.93 (verified two ways: dpsgd.gaussian(1.0) composed 1000x = 633.930, single Gaussian at nm/sqrt(1000) = 633.983). That is a 145x under-report, growing as sqrt(n_steps). The charge is flat in max_participations: at n_steps=32, min_sep=4, nm=1.0 the reported epsilon is 4.3772 for k = 1, 2, 4 and 8, while band_mf_strategy(bands=8) at the same settings correctly rises to 7.8394/12.9407/20.8267. The parameter is accepted and silently discarded -- no warning, no rejection. Not fully silent at the documentation level: docs/reference/accounting.md:420-421 warns against exactly this bare call, so a careful reader is steered away; a reader who follows the immediately preceding paragraph ('max_participations defaults to n_steps ... do not compose it again by the number of rounds') is not. Tracked as acceptance criterion 1 of open issue #359.

tracked.title: Paired second-moment MF release is never tied to an accountant; a documented mismatched-strategy pair is 1.31x under-noised relative to the charged budget
tracked.reasoning: Every link verified. _second_moment.py:139-150 pins both column norms at the single-participation schema (c1/c2 requested with min_sep=n_steps, max_participations=1) and calls paired_noise_stddevs(noise_multiplier / c1, first=max_norm*c1, second=squared_max_norm*c2). noise_allocation.py:252-255 makes the joint Mahalanobis budget exactly (c1/nm)^2 at the single-participation sensitivities, which matches MfGaussian.pld(nm, c1) -- but under a k-participation schema the realized budget becomes (c1/nm)^2 * (D1*c1*r1^2 + D2*c2*r2^2)/(D1*c1 + D2*c2) with r_i = S_k^(i)/c_i, while _mf_gaussian.py:132-140 charges (S_k^(1)/nm)^2 and MfGaussian has no second-strategy field; I re-derived this algebra independently and it matches. I grepped the whole dpftrl accounting tree: no second-moment- or paired-aware accountant exists anywhere, and _mf_gaussian_noise.py:65,119-127 type-checks second_moment_strategy but never compares it to the first. Reproduced numerically by spying on the real runtime call: n_steps=64, min_sep=8, max_participations=8, nm=3.0, both streams max_norm=1.0, first=band_mf_strategy(bands=8), second=bisr_strategy(bandwidth=8) -> paired_noise_stddevs is called as (3.0, first=1.0, second=1.0) and deploys sigma1 = sigma2 = 4.2426; measured strategy sensitivities band_mf 1.0/1.4142/2.0/2.8284 and bisr 1.0/1.9658/3.0026/4.4161 at k=1/2/4/8, so r1=2.8284, r2=4.4161; realized joint budget 1.527902 vs charged 0.888889, ratio 1.71889, sqrt 1.31106. Translated to epsilon: the accountant reports the Gaussian at nm/S_k = 1.0607 -> eps 4.089 at delta=1e-5, while the deployed release is the Gaussian at 0.8090 -> eps 5.605, a 1.37x epsilon under-report. Docs quotes verified verbatim (noise.md:304-307 blesses a differing second-moment workload; dp-ftrl.md:176-178 asserts the joint allocation is accounted with the same mechanism PLD as the first-moment release). Severity lowered from high to medium: the defect needs an opt-in paired second-moment release (second_moment_strategy must be passed explicitly -- a paired input without it raises) AND two strategies with different participation growth factors AND r2 > r1; with the same strategy on both streams r1 == r2 and the accounting is exact, and when r1 > r2 the error is conservative. Magnitude at the measured config is 1.31x in effective noise multiplier / 1.37x in epsilon, not orders of magnitude. This is acceptance criterion 2 of OPEN issue #359 ('Runtime first/second-moment allocation and accounting use the same deployed sensitivities'), as the finding itself states.

tracked.title: activation_offloading copies model weights, not only activations, on every microbatch
tracked.reasoning: Code chain verified line by line in the current tree. packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/torch/checkpoint/save_on_cpu.py:29-35 packs every saved tensor with `tensor.cpu()` and no size/role/alias test; the patch is live on the pinned torch (2.14.0+cu130) because native_support.saved_tensor_hooks_guard_scoped() returns False, so packages/.../checkpoint/__init__.py:52 calls save_on_cpu.apply(). _dp_trainer.py:1423-1430 builds `save_on_cpu(pin_memory=False)` when args.activation_offloading, and _dp_trainer.py:2204 wraps the whole `ctx.grad_fn(...)` (vmap(grad)+clip) in it. Reproduced the packing behavior on CPU with a saved_tensors_hooks probe: for nn.Sequential(Linear(64,256), ReLU, Linear(256,32)) under vmap(grad(functional_call)), 8 tensors are packed and the (256,32) second-layer weight (32768 B) is among them, packed unbatched -> once per grad_fn call regardless of microbatch size. Also reproduced the LoRA-shaped case: with only tiny adapters differentiated, every FROZEN base weight is still packed (needed for grad-wrt-input), ~1.5x the base parameter bytes per microbatch. So the mechanism the finding describes is real: enabling activation_offloading moves on the order of the (non-first-layer) parameter set device->host->device per microbatch, pageable, in addition to activations. TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding. (1) The first layer's weight is NOT saved (its input gradient is not needed), so the traffic is the parameter set minus the first layer, not literally every F.linear weight. (2) The 'dominant term' quantification is NOT established and its measurement is methodologically wrong: the cited 69,632 B / 94% figure counts tensor.numel()*element_size() as seen inside the functorch levels, i.e. per-example LOGICAL shapes. Unwrapping to the physical tensors (torch._C._functorch.get_unwrapped) shows activation tensors carry the microbatch dimension while the weight does not, so the weight share falls with microbatch size: on that same model I measured 36360 B total / 90% weight at B=1, 47136 B / 70% at B=4, 90240 B / 36% at B=16; in the LoRA probe 60% at B=1 vs 19% at B=8. Analytically the activation/weight ratio scales like microbatch*seq_len/hidden, so at realistic sequence lengths the parameter term is a meaningful but usually not dominant fraction. Severity lowered to low: performance only (affects_epsilon false, gradients verified identical with and without the hooks), reachable only via activation_offloading=True which defaults to False (_training_arguments.py:545), and already covered by an open tracked issue. DUPLICATE: issue #969 ('Make activation offload selective and overlap transfers', open, milestone Bazalt) cites the same two code sites, states the hook 'copies every saved tensor to CPU ... including small values, cheap-to-recompute tensors, parameter aliases', proposes exactly the fix sketched here ('selection policy based on tensor size, role/storage alias ... Keep parameter storage and tiny/cheap tensors on device'), and already records the same failure mode ('Offloading everything ... can be slower than reducing microbatch size'). PR #994 'perf(functional): make activation offload selective' is closed unmerged and the tree still has no policy. Not verified: any GPU wall-clock or PCIe measurement, and the host-RSS growth claim - no CUDA device is available in this environment.
tracked.corrected_failure_scenario: With activation_offloading=True (non-default), DPTrainer wraps the whole vmap(grad)+clip call in save_on_cpu(pin_memory=False). Because F.linear saves its weight whenever the gradient with respect to its input is needed, every parameter except the first layer's - including frozen base weights in a LoRA run - is copied device->host->device once per microbatch through pageable host memory, on top of the activations. Reproduced on CPU with a saved_tensors_hooks probe: unbatched weight tensors appear in the packed set and their byte volume is independent of microbatch size, whereas activation bytes scale with it (weight share of packed physical bytes: 90% at microbatch 1, 36% at microbatch 16 on a 2-layer MLP; 60% vs 19% in a LoRA-shaped probe). The consequence is wasted PCIe traffic on the order of the parameter set per microbatch that offloading was never meant to pay - a throughput regression, not a correctness or privacy defect - and it is a meaningful but generally not dominant fraction of total transfer at realistic sequence lengths. No GPU timing was measured.

refuted.title: GPT-2 is the documented quick-start model and a listed compatible family, but its per-example gradients diverge from upstream by 53x relative error
refuted.reasoning: The premise - that patched GPT-2's per-example gradients materially diverge from the model's true gradients - does not hold. The 53x relative error is the same number I reproduce, but it is an artifact of the parity harness, not of the patched model. The harness compares an unpatched reference running GPT-2's default stochastic training dropout (resid_pdrop=embd_pdrop=attn_pdrop=0.1, never zeroed by the tiny config) against a patched model whose dropout the `dropout` compat patch zeroes by design (_router.py:161-168 -> components/dropout.py disable_dropout, on by default under compat=True; its docstring gives the rationale: DP-SGD trains without dropout and SDPA's fused dropout is vmap-incompatible). Measured: the patched model in .train() returns an identical loss on repeated draws equal to its .eval() loss (4.912911415 x3), while the unpatched reference varies per draw. Once the reference gets the same dropout-free contract (attn_pdrop=embd_pdrop=resid_pdrop=0.0), assert_parity_grad and assert_parity_vmap_grad both PASS and 0 of 16 gradients differ under torch.equal - bit-exact, not merely within tolerance. So a user following the HF quick start on gpt2 does not get materially wrong per-example gradients; they get exactly upstream's gradients for a dropout-free model, which is the intended DP training contract for every family, not something specific to gpt2. Maintainers reached the same conclusion: open PR #1032 (closing #813) states 'The GPT-2 mismatch came from comparing its default stochastic training dropout against Opaque's deterministic DP model preparation ... restoring backward and clipped vmap(grad) parity without changing GPT-2 model behavior or support', and fixes the harness rather than the model. Residue: (a) the docs-vs-skipped-test optics, already owned by open #813; (b) a minor docs gap - docs/user-guide/huggingface/model-patches.md:58 enumerates the compat bucket as eager_attention/batchify/vmap_masking/empty_batches/vmap_checkpointing and never mentions that compat=True also zeroes all model dropout (only docs/alignment/trainers.md:202 and docs/reference/transformers.md:570 document a disable_dropout flag, for the alignment trainers). Neither supports a high-severity 'silently wrong training' claim, and the fix_sketch's de-register-gpt2 recommendation would act on a false diagnosis.
refuted.corrected_failure_scenario: No reproducible defect. Patched GPT-2's backward and clipped vmap(grad) gradients are bit-identical to upstream once both sides use the same dropout rate (0/16 parameters differ under torch.equal); the quoted abs_err=1.93e-02 / rel_err=5.30e+01 comes from the harness comparing a dropout-0.1 reference against a patched model whose dropout the default `dropout` compat patch intentionally zeroes. The residual, much smaller issue is documentation: model-patches.md:58 does not list dropout-zeroing among the compat-bucket effects, so a reader cannot tell that apply_model_patches(compat=True) removes dropout from their model. The docs-promote-gpt2-while-its-parity-tests-are-skipped optics are already tracked by open #813, whose open PR #1032 removes the gpt2 grad exemptions entirely.
